signals.title: Long-running bash commands with large outputs cause truncation and agent retry loops
signals.text: ### Description Long-running bash commands with verbose output are being truncated and/or timed out, causing agents to re-attempt commands instead of polling the saved tool output. This creates serious idempotency issues in workflows where commands should run to completion. **Current behavior:** 1. Bash commands have a hardcoded 2-minute default timeout (`src/tool/bash.ts:21`) 2. Output is truncated at 2,000 lines or 50KB (`src/tool/truncation.ts:10-11`) 3. When output is truncated, full output is saved to `~/.opencode/data/tool-output/`, but agents frequently re-run the command instead of reading the saved output 4. Commands are killed after timeout, even if they would have completed successfully **The problem:** - Commands that produce large build logs, test outputs, or verbose diagnostics get truncated - Agents see truncated output and often retry the command instead of using `Read` with offset/limit on the saved output file - This creates duplicate work, wasted API calls, and potential side effects from non-idempotent commands - For CI/CD workflows, this behavior is unacceptable - commands should never exit until a proper exit code is received **Current configuration options:** - `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` - env var for timeout (exists) - No configuration for `MAX_LINES` or `MAX_BYTES` truncation limits (hardcoded) **Proposed solution:** Add `opencode.json` configuration for these limits: ```jsonc { "experimental": { "bash": { "timeout_ms": 600000, // 10 minutes "max_lines": 10000, // or null to disable "max_bytes": 512000 // or null to disable } } } ``` This would allow users to configure behavior appropriate for their workflows without needing environment variables. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version Current (main branch) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run a command that produces more than 2,000 lines of output (e.g., `npm install` with verbose logging, large test suite) 2. Observe output is truncated with message about saved file 3. Watch agent retry the command instead of reading the saved output 4. For timeout: run any command that takes longer than 2 minutes ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System macOS ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: CLI/TUI multi-file apply_patch approval only shows first file diff
signals.text: ### Description In CLI/TUI mode, when an agent uses `apply_patch` with changes across multiple files, the approval/review UI only displays one file's diff instead of rendering every changed file. `apply_patch` already returns structured per-file diff metadata, but the permission UI still renders the request as a single `edit` diff blob. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start an interactive CLI/TUI session. 2. Ask the agent to use `apply_patch` on 2 or more files in one patch. 3. Wait for the edit permission/approval prompt. 4. Inspect the rendered diff. ### Expected behavior The approval UI shows a separate diff block for each changed file in the patch. ### Actual behavior Only one file's diff is displayed, even though the patch touches multiple files. ### Likely cause - `packages/opencode/src/tool/apply_patch.ts` already populates `metadata.files` for each changed file. - `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/routes/session/permission.tsx` handles edit permissions by reading only `metadata.diff` / `metadata.filepath`, so multi-file `apply_patch` requests are rendered as a single diff view instead of iterating `metadata.files`. - There is already a multi-file renderer for completed `apply_patch` results in `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/routes/session/index.tsx`, which suggests the permission path is the missing piece. - `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts` also appears to lack explicit `apply_patch` handling, so non-interactive CLI output falls back to generic tool rendering. ### Suggested fix - In `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/routes/session/permission.tsx`, render `request.metadata.files` when present, with a per-file diff block and fallback to the existing single-file edit behavior. - In `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts`, add explicit `apply_patch` rendering that uses `metadata.files` when available.

signals.title: Stale stdin bytes leak to shell after exit on POSIX (space on prompt, blocks ctrl+d)
signals.text: ## Description After exiting opencode on Linux/macOS, stale bytes sometimes remain in the kernel's tty input buffer and are read by the parent shell. The most common symptom is a space character appearing on the shell prompt line, which blocks `ctrl+d` (EOF) from terminating the shell since readline requires an empty line. ## Related Issues - #12257 — residual output after exit (Alacritty + tmux + Fish) - #7861 — terminal unusable after exit on macOS - #15084 — garbled characters ("ppppp") after Ctrl+C exit on macOS - #5070 — escape codes leak after exit on Windows (git bash) - #8395 — PowerShell terminal hangs after `/exit` ## Root Cause During `@opentui/core`'s `finalizeDestroy()`, the stdin data listener is removed and raw mode is disabled, but the kernel's tty input buffer is not flushed. Any bytes that arrived between the last stdin read and the mode switch (e.g. key release events from the Kitty keyboard protocol, or other in-flight terminal data) persist in the cooked-mode line discipline buffer. When the process exits, the shell inherits these bytes. On Windows this was already handled — `win32FlushInputBuffer()` calls `FlushConsoleInputBuffer` via kernel32 FFI after `renderer.destroy()`. There was no POSIX equivalent. Notably, `@opentui/core`'s own `resume()` method drains stdin (`while (this.stdin.read() !== null) {}`), but `finalizeDestroy()` does not — nor does it call `stdin.pause()` like `suspend()` does. ## Fix Add a cross-platform `flushInputBuffer()` that calls `tcflush(STDIN_FILENO, TCIFLUSH)` on POSIX via libc FFI (`libc.so.6` on Linux, `libSystem.B.dylib` on macOS), alongside the existing Windows `FlushConsoleInputBuffer` path. Call it after `renderer.destroy()` in both exit paths (`exit.tsx` and the `ErrorComponent` in `app.tsx`). Also rename `win32.ts` → `console.ts` since it now contains cross-platform code, and drop the `win32` prefix from `flushInputBuffer` (the two Windows-only functions retain their prefix). ## Environment - **OS:** Linux (also affects macOS) - **Terminal:** Konsole (likely affects most terminals) - **Shell:** Any (readline sees the stale bytes)

signals.title: Cost tracking ($ Spent) does not work for custom provider models
signals.text: ### Problem When using a custom provider configured via `opencode.jsonc` with `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, the UI does not track or display **$ Spent**. The cost remains at `$0.00` regardless of token usage. Built-in providers get their pricing data from [models.dev](https://models.dev) and cost tracking works for those. For custom providers, the `cost` config fields are available in the schema but do not appear to have any effect on the UI. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure a custom provider in `opencode.jsonc` with `cost` fields specified per the config schema: ```jsonc { "provider": { "my-provider": { "name": "My Provider", "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "models": { "my-model": { "name": "My Model", "cost": { "input": 0.0000055, "output": 0.0000275, "cache_read": 5.5e-7, "cache_write": 0.000006875 }, "limit": { "context": 200000, "output": 64000, "input": 200000 }, "tool_call": true } }, "options": { "baseURL": "https://my-proxy.example.com" } } } } ``` 2. Start a session using the custom provider model. 3. Send messages and observe the cost display in the UI. ### Expected Behavior The UI calculates and displays a running cost using the `cost` values defined in the model config and the token usage from the response. ### Actual Behavior $ Spent remains at `$0.00` for the entire session. The `cost` config fields on custom provider models have no observable effect. ### Environment - Custom provider backed by a LiteLLM proxy via `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` - Multiple models tested — issue is consistent across all custom provider models - `cost` structure matches the config JSON schema at `https://opencode.ai/config.json`, including `input`, `output`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`, and `context_over_200k` sub-fields

signals.title: [FEATURE]:add spinnerVerbs config to customize TUI spinner text
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Feature Request ### Summary Allow users to customize the verb displayed next to the spinner in the TUI via `opencode.json`, similar to Claude Code's `spinnerVerbs` setting. ### Motivation Claude Code supports a `spinnerVerbs` config that lets users replace or append to the default loading verbs shown while the model is thinking (e.g. "Thinking...", "Working..."). This is a small quality-of-life feature that makes the tool feel more personalized and fun. opencode currently only lets you suppress the spinner entirely (`-q`), with no way to customize the text shown in interactive TUI mode. ### Proposed API Add a `spinnerVerbs` key to `opencode.json`: ```json { "spinnerVerbs": { "mode": "replace", "verbs": ["Hallucinating", "Vibing", "Summoning demons"] } } ``` **Fields:** - `mode`: - `"replace"` — use only the provided verbs - `"append"` — add to the existing default verbs - `verbs`: array of strings, each displayed (with `"..."` appended) while the model is processing ### Implementation sketch The spinner component (likely somewhere under `internal/tui/` or similar) would need to: 1. Read `spinnerVerbs` from the config struct (add field to whatever struct mirrors `opencode.json`) 2. On init, build the verb list based on `mode`: - `replace` → use only user-provided verbs - `append` → append user verbs to the default list 3. Cycle through verbs on each spinner tick (same as current behavior, just with the configurable list) No behavior change when `spinnerVerbs` is absent — fully backwards compatible. ### Prior art - Claude Code `settings.json`: `spinnerVerbs.mode` + `spinnerVerbs.verbs`

signals.title: Memory Megathread
signals.text: We have scattered reports of memory issues so we are going to tackle them all in a central place. PLEASE DO NOT RUN YOUR LLM AND SUGGEST SOLUTIONS IT IS ALWAYS WRONG What we need help with is collecting heap snapshots. There are two ways to do that. Manual snapshot flow - run opencode (terminal not desktop) - use it until memory has grown (we don't need crazy numbers, once it hits 1-2gb it should help) - press ctrl+p and select heap snapshot - ui will freeze while it is generated - upload generated files [here](https://www.dropbox.com/request/njJ07VcjIb0wPQ50ARe2) - leave a comment describing your issue a bit Automatic snapshot flow - run opencode with `OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1`, for example `OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1 opencode` - use it until memory grows past around 2gb - opencode checks memory once a minute and automatically writes a heap snapshot when rss is above 2gb - snapshots are written to the log directory as `.heapsnapshot` files - upload generated files [here](https://www.dropbox.com/request/njJ07VcjIb0wPQ50ARe2) - leave a comment describing your issue a bit and mention that you used the automatic flow If you follow this we can almost always trace the issue and fix it

signals.title: opencode export can write session JSON that opencode import cannot read in 1.4.3
signals.text: ## Summary `opencode 1.4.3` can export a session JSON file that `opencode 1.4.3` cannot import again. The failure happens with sessions that still contain legacy pre-1.4 data shapes. `export` appears to serialize that legacy shape as-is, while `import` validates against the new 1.4 schema. ## Version ```bash opencode --version # 1.4.3 ``` ## Repro 1. Export an existing session: ```bash sid=$(opencode session list --format json -n 1 | jq -r '.[0].id') opencode export "$sid" > /tmp/session.json ``` 2. Try to import the exported file: ```bash opencode import /tmp/session.json ``` ## Actual result Import fails with: ```json [ { "expected": "string", "code": "invalid_type", "path": ["summary", "diffs", 0, "patch"], "message": "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined" } ] ``` I also see legacy user message fields like top-level `variant` in the exported JSON. ## Expected result A file produced by `opencode export` should be importable by `opencode import` in the same version. ## What I found The exported file contains legacy-shaped data such as: - `messages[].info.variant` instead of `messages[].info.model.variant` - `summary.diffs[*].before/after` without `patch` I wrote a local converter that: - moves `messages[].info.variant` -> `messages[].info.model.variant` - replaces legacy `summary.diffs[*].before/after` with a schema-valid `patch` string After that conversion, `opencode import` succeeds. ## Important follow-up finding Even after importing the converted JSON successfully, re-exporting that same session still produces legacy-shaped data again, and raw re-import fails again. So import success does **not** appear to normalize the stored session permanently. ## Evidence from one real session On my exported session JSON: - legacy user `variant` fields: `53` - legacy diff entries with `before/after` and no `patch`: `73` After converting the JSON file, import succeeds. After importing the converted file and re-exporting that same session: - legacy user `variant` fields: `53` - legacy diff entries with `before/after` and no `patch`: `73` And raw import fails again with the same `summary.diffs[0].patch` error. ## Likely cause `export` appears to serialize raw stored session data without normalizing legacy shapes, while `import` strictly validates against current schemas. So either: 1. `export` should normalize legacy session/message data before writing JSON, or 2. `import` should accept and migrate legacy export shapes, or 3. both ## Relevant code paths These looked relevant when I checked source: - `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/export.ts` - `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/import.ts` - `packages/opencode/src/snapshot/index.ts` - `packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts`
signals.author: christianknauer

signals.title: [Bug]: XDG Base Directory Spec violation — node_modules installed in ~/.config instead of ~/.local/share
signals.text: ### Description When running `opencode`, the application installs runtime dependencies (`node_modules`, `package.json`, and `package-lock.json`) into `~/.config/opencode`. This is a violation of the [XDG Base Directory Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html). The `~/.config` directory (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) is strictly reserved for user-specific configuration files. Runtime data, dependencies, and state files should be stored in `~/.local/share` (`$XDG_DATA_HOME`). ### Why this is a problem - Many users back up their `~/.config` directory using tools like `git` (dotfiles), `stow`, or `chezmoi`. Placing `node_modules` in this directory causes massive repository bloat, sync issues, and forces users to manually add workarounds to their `.gitignore` files. - **Broken File Watchers:** Applications, background daemons, or text editors that monitor `~/.config` for configuration changes get overwhelmed or stuck in infinite reload loops due to the massive number of files and rapid I/O operations within `node_modules`. - **Loss of Configuration Portability:** Mixing mutable runtime dependencies with immutable configuration files breaks portability across different environments (Linux, macOS). It prevents users from symlinking their configs using tools like `stow`, as the application attempts to write heavy runtime data directly into the clean config structure. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.15.0 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Launch `opencode`. 2. Check the contents of the config directory: `ls ~/.config/opencode`. 3. Notice that `node_modules`, `package.json`, and `package-lock.json` are created there. ### Expected behavior - Configuration files stay in `~/.config/opencode/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/`). - Runtime dependencies, packages, and downloaded data should be placed in `~/.local/share/opencode/` (or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/`). ### Actual behavior Runtime dependencies and package tracking files are placed in `~/.config/opencode/`. ### Operating System Arch Linux ### Terminal Ghostty
signals.author: ilyachch

signals.title: v1.15.1+ Breaks Bun Installs
signals.text: ### Description I see that [v1.15.1](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v1.15.1) now requires postinstall lifecycle scripts to run. Most package managers that aren't NPM block this by default these days. Bun doesn't allow users to run postinstall scripts for global packages. Another issue is that `bin/opencode.exe` (renamed from `opencode` in v1.15.1) can't be executed directly under Linux (and I'm assuming Windows?) - so executing opencode just returns an exec error. ``` echo "Error: opencode-ai's postinstall script was not run." >&2 echo "" >&2 echo "This occurs when using --ignore-scripts during installation, or when using a" >&2 echo "package manager like pnpm that does not run postinstall scripts by default." >&2 echo "" >&2 echo "To fix this, run the postinstall script manually:" >&2 echo " cd node_modules/opencode-ai && node postinstall.mjs" >&2 echo "" >&2 echo "Or reinstall opencode-ai without the --ignore-scripts flag." >&2 exit 1 ``` ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.15.3 ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Debian 13 ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: Bug: Los subagentes heredan permisos deny del agente primario via deriveSubagentSessionPermission(), sobrescribiendo sus propios allow (regresion desde v1.14.46)
signals.text: ﻿## Descripcion Cuando se usa la herramienta `task` para delegar trabajo a un subagente, el subagente hereda TODAS las reglas `deny` del agente primario a traves de `deriveSubagentSessionPermission()`. Debido a la evaluacion "ultima coincidencia gana" (last-match-wins), estas reglas `deny` heredadas sobrescriben los permisos `allow` explicitos que el subagente tiene definidos en su frontmatter YAML. Esto rompe efectivamente el patron commander+worker: un agente primario con permisos restringidos (ej: `edit: deny`) no puede delegar tareas de escritura a un subagente que tiene `edit: allow` en su propia configuracion. ## Pasos para reproducir 1. Configurar un agente primario con `edit: deny` en `opencode.jsonc`: ```json { "permission": { "edit": "deny" } } ``` 2. Crear un subagente con `edit: allow` en su frontmatter: ```yaml --- name: mi-escritor mode: subagent permission: edit: allow --- ``` 3. Desde el agente primario, delegar una tarea al subagente via `task` 4. El subagente NO tendra la herramienta `write` disponible, a pesar de tener `edit: allow` en su propio frontmatter. ## Comportamiento esperado Los permisos explicitos de un subagente deberian tener prioridad sobre los permisos heredados del agente primario. Si un subagente tiene `edit: allow` en su frontmatter, deberia tener acceso a las herramientas `write`, `edit` y `apply_patch` independientemente de los permisos del agente primario. ## Comportamiento actual El subagente hereda las reglas `deny` del agente primario. Debido a la evaluacion last-match-wins, el `deny` heredado sobrescribe el `allow` del subagente. La herramienta `write` (y otras herramientas de edicion) no estan disponibles para el subagente. ## Analisis tecnico El bug esta en `deriveSubagentSessionPermission()` en `packages/opencode/src/agent/subagent-permissions.ts`, que: 1. Filtra las reglas `deny` del agente padre con `parentAgent.permission.filter(rule => rule.action === "deny" && rule.permission === "edit")` 2. Las anade al conjunto de permisos de la sesion del subagente 3. El runtime evalua `Permission.merge(subagent.permission, session.permission)` en `packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts` (linea 267) 4. Como `Permission.merge()` hace `rulesets.flat()`, y las reglas `deny` heredadas aparecen DESPUES de las reglas `allow` del subagente en el array, la evaluacion last-match-wins hace que ganen los `deny` ## Issues relacionados - #26700 — "Subagent parent deny inheritance over-constrains delegated agents with explicit permissions" (cerrado, el fix fue parcial) - #26758 — "Bug: Subagents no longer have access to tools (in commander+worker pattern)" (cerrado) - #26873 — "[BUG] Subagent keeps parent agent permissions" (cerrado) - #27123 — "[FEATURE]: Insane. Add independent agents back." (cerrado) - #27886 — "Subagent can call plan_exit to escape plan mode" (abierto, v1.15.3) - PR #26597 — "fix(task): subagent inherits parent agent's deny rules" (fusionado, introdujo la regresion) La regresion original se introdujo en **v1.14.46** por el PR #26597 (fix para #26514: "Subagents Bypass Plan Mode READ-ONLY Restrictions"). El issue #26700 se suponia que arreglaria esto pero el fix parece incompleto — sigue heredando los `deny` del padre. ## Workaround Actualmente, el unico workaround es NO usar `deny` en el agente primario para los permisos que los subagentes necesitan. Usar `ask` en lugar de `deny` permite que los subagentes hereden `ask` que su propio `allow` puede sobrescribir. Sin embargo, esto no es ideal para configuraciones orientadas a seguridad donde el agente primario no deberia tener capacidades de edicion. ## Entorno - Version de OpenCode: 1.15.3 - SO: Windows (nativo, no WSL) - Patron de agentes: Coordinador primario con `edit: deny` + subagentes con `edit: allow`
signals.author: ROKO108

signals.title: writeOsc52 broken under GNU screen — uses tmux DCS format, no chunking
signals.text: ### Description `writeOsc52` in `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/util/clipboard.ts` treats GNU screen and tmux the same way, wrapping both in `\x1bPtmux;\x1b...\x1b\\`. This was originally reported by @valdemardi in #26491 / #26492 (closed before merging). The `tmux;` prefix is specific to tmux. Under screen, it is output verbatim alongside the escape sequences. The embedded OSC52 usually still reaches the clipboard (`\x1b]52;c;...\x07` is valid enough), but the `tmux;` garbage and leaked escape sequences corrupt the terminal output and scramble the TUI display. Screen also has a 768-byte DCS buffer limit (`MAXSTR`), so clipboard writes larger than ~750 bytes are silently truncated. Screen requires chunking with `\x1b\\\x1bP` between segments. ### Plugins N/A ### OpenCode version 1.15.6 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run inside a GNU screen session (`STY` is set) 2. Try any clipboard copy 3. Text may reach the clipboard but the TUI display gets corrupted with garbage characters and escape artifacts ### Screenshot and/or share link N/A ### Operating System Linux ### Terminal Alacritty and GNU screen v5
signals.author: lingfish

signals.title: @ file mention never shows project files on Windows — only agents (general/explore) appear
signals.text: **[BUG] @ file mention never shows project files on Windows — only agents (general/explore) appear** **OpenCode version:** 1.15.7 **Platform:** Windows (win32, Windows 10/11) **Shell:** PowerShell 7.6.1 (pwsh) **Terminal:** VS Code integrated terminal + standalone PowerShell (both affected) --- ## Summary Typing `@` in the TUI prompt only shows agent suggestions (`@general`, `@explore`). Project files never appear, regardless of whether I type just `@` or `@` followed by search text. The `opencode debug file tree` command fails with "Unexpected error". ## Environment - **Project size:** 18,103 files - **Key directories:** `build/` (10,607 files), `.git/` (4,759 files), `src/` (769 files), `external/` (888 files) - **File watcher:** `platform=win32 backend=windows` ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Navigate to a project with 18,000+ files 2. Run `opencode` 3. Type `@` in the prompt 4. Only agents appear — no file suggestions ## What I've Tried 1. Cleared OpenCode cache (`%USERPROFILE%\.cache\opencode`) — no change 2. Added `watcher.ignore` to `opencode.json` excluding `build/**`, `.git/**`, `.cache/**`, `.vs/**` — no change 3. Restarted OpenCode multiple times — no change 4. Tried `opencode --log-level DEBUG --pure` — same result 5. Tried both just `@` and `@` followed by filename text — neither shows files 6. Tried VS Code extension AND standalone PowerShell terminal — both affected ## Diagnostic Evidence **Log confirms watcher initializes but never publishes file tree:** ``` file.watcher directory=C:\...\project init file.watcher platform=win32 backend=windows watcher backend ``` No `file.tree.updated`, `mention`, or `autocomplete` events appear in logs. **`opencode debug file tree` fails:** ``` Error: Unexpected error, check log file at ... ``` **`opencode debug file list` works** — server CAN see files, but TUI mention system doesn't receive them. **`opencode debug file status` works** — returns git file status correctly. **Resolved config shows watcher ignore patterns are applied:** ```json { "watcher": { "ignore": ["build/**", "build-serena/**", ".git/**", ".cache/**", ".vs/**"] } } ``` ## Expected Behavior `@` should fuzzy-search project files and show them alongside agents in the mention dropdown. ## Actual Behavior Only agents appear. File index/tree is never populated.

signals.title: Orphaned index.lock in snapshot gitdir causes blocking snapshot queue on Windows (Git Bash / mintty)
signals.text: ### Description When OpenCode is terminated ungracefully (for example: closing mintty, Ctrl+C during execution, or abrupt terminal shutdown), the internal snapshot repository under: ~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/// can be left with a stale/orphaned index.lock file. On subsequent runs, snapshot operations such as git add --sparse block waiting for the git lock timeout (~12–15s per attempt on Windows/git). Since snapshot operations appear to be serialized through a per-gitdir semaphore/mutex, the entire snapshot pipeline becomes blocked. This causes OpenCode to appear frozen or extremely slow: prompt submitted model header appears no response for long periods high CPU/disk activity no visible error message The issue is especially reproducible on Windows + Git Bash (mintty), likely because abrupt terminal shutdowns can interrupt git operations without cleanup. Important: GitHub Copilot authentication works correctly API requests work correctly outside OpenCode (verified with curl + streaming) Running in smaller repositories improves responsiveness Running from HOME directories worsens the issue significantly Observed code behavior The git runner appears to swallow git failures silently: B.catch((R) => B.succeed({ code: ExitCode(1), text: "", stderr: ... })) This makes the failure invisible to the user and difficult to diagnose. Steps to reproduce Run OpenCode from Git Bash (mintty) on Windows Interrupt execution abruptly: close mintty window or Ctrl+C during snapshot activity Run: opencode run "hello" Observe long hangs/blocking behavior Expected behavior OpenCode should: detect stale/orphaned index.lock files automatically clean old locks or at minimum surface a clear snapshot/git error Actual behavior OpenCode becomes extremely slow or appears frozen until the lock is manually removed. Current workaround find ~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot -name "index.lock" -delete Suggested fix Before snapshot git operations (git add, git write-tree, etc.), detect stale locks: const lockPath = path.join(gitdir, "index.lock"); if (await fs.exists(lockPath)) { const stat = await fs.stat(lockPath); if (Date.now() - stat.mtimeMs > 30_000) { await fs.rm(lockPath); } } ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version Version: 1.15.10 (Windows x64) ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link When OpenCode is terminated ungracefully (for example: closing mintty, Ctrl+C during execution, or abrupt terminal shutdown), the internal snapshot repository under: ~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/// can be left with a stale/orphaned index.lock file. On subsequent runs, snapshot operations such as git add --sparse block waiting for the git lock timeout (~12–15s per attempt on Windows/git). Since snapshot operations appear to be serialized through a per-gitdir semaphore/mutex, the entire snapshot pipeline becomes blocked. This causes OpenCode to appear frozen or extremely slow: prompt submitted model header appears no response for long periods high CPU/disk activity no visible error message The issue is especially reproducible on Windows + Git Bash (mintty), likely because abrupt terminal shutdowns can interrupt git operations without cleanup. Important: GitHub Copilot authentication works correctly API requests work correctly outside OpenCode (verified with curl + streaming) Running in smaller repositories improves responsiveness Running from HOME directories worsens the issue significantly Observed code behavior The git runner appears to swallow git failures silently: B.catch((R) => B.succeed({ code: ExitCode(1), text: "", stderr: ... })) This makes the failure invisible to the user and difficult to diagnose. Steps to reproduce Run OpenCode from Git Bash (mintty) on Windows Interrupt execution abruptly: close mintty window or Ctrl+C during snapshot activity Run: opencode run "hello" Observe long hangs/blocking behavior Expected behavior OpenCode should: detect stale/orphaned index.lock files automatically clean old locks or at minimum surface a clear snapshot/git error Actual behavior OpenCode becomes extremely slow or appears frozen until the lock is manually removed. Current workaround find ~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot -name "index.lock" -delete Suggested fix Before snapshot git operations (git add, git write-tree, etc.), detect stale locks: const lockPath = path.join(gitdir, "index.lock"); if (await fs.exists(lockPath)) { const stat = await fs.stat(lockPath); if (Date.now() - stat.mtimeMs > 30_000) { await fs.rm(lockPath); } } ### Operating System Windows 11 Git Bash (mintty) GitHub Copilot provider ### Terminal Git Bash (mintty terminal) running on Windows 11

Running `echo $TERM_PROGRAM` correctly outputs `vscode`. 6. signals.title: Session token usage grows unbounded via cache.read and causes unrecoverable context-window errors
signals.text: ### Description Long-running sessions can grow their recorded token usage without a practical upper bound, especially through `tokens.cache.read`, until most models/providers fail with a context-window error and the session becomes unrecoverable. In my real session, OpenCode reported approximately **56,128,248 total tokens** while the persisted conversation data was small: ```text session tokens: input: 14,774,671 output: 77,881 reasoning: 20,400 cache.read: 41,255,296 cache.write: 0 total: 56,128,248 stored rows for that session: message: 224 rows, ~0.52 MB JSON data part: 1042 rows, ~2.33 MB JSON data ``` After this, continuing the same session fails with: ```text Your input exceeds the context window of this model. Please adjust your input and try again. ``` The issue is not that the saved message JSON itself is tens of millions of tokens. The large number appears to come from cumulative session usage accounting. In particular, `tokens_cache_read` can grow very large over repeated turns. Relevant code path observed in source: ```text packages/core/src/session/projector.ts tokens_input: SessionTable.tokens_input + value.tokens.input tokens_output: SessionTable.tokens_output + value.tokens.output tokens_reasoning: SessionTable.tokens_reasoning + value.tokens.reasoning tokens_cache_read: SessionTable.tokens_cache_read + value.tokens.cache.read tokens_cache_write: SessionTable.tokens_cache_write + value.tokens.cache.write ``` This makes session-level usage an ever-growing lifetime counter. That is fine for statistics, but it becomes dangerous if any compaction / routing / provider request / context-window logic treats cumulative session usage, especially `cache.read`, as if it represented the current prompt/context size. Impact: - Long sessions eventually hit provider context-window errors. - Auto compaction does not reliably save an already-overflowed session. - Once overflowed, the same session can repeatedly fail and effectively becomes unusable. - `opencode stats` can become slow/hang on large databases/sessions. - This affects providers/models with smaller context windows especially badly when using an `auto` model/router. Expected behavior: - Current context-window checks should be based on the actual messages that will be sent to the provider, not lifetime cumulative usage counters. - `cache.read` should not be counted as current prompt/context tokens for overflow decisions. - Auto compaction should trigger before the provider rejects the request. - If a provider returns a known context-window error, OpenCode should attempt a safe compact/prune/retry or suggest/fork a new session instead of leaving the session dead. - There should be a hard cap / safety guard for long-running sessions, e.g. archive/fork/reset usage or force compaction before sending. ### Plugins Only a local/custom provider/router was used (`providerID: 9090`, `modelID: auto`). No plugin-specific behavior is required to reproduce the core issue: repeated turns can accumulate session usage far beyond any real model context window. ### OpenCode version 1.15.13 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use OpenCode with a provider/model that reports token usage including cache read tokens. 2. Keep a long-running session active for many turns, especially with repeated cache hits or provider-side prompt caching. 3. Inspect the SQLite session row, for example: ```sql select tokens_input, tokens_output, tokens_reasoning, tokens_cache_read, tokens_cache_write from session where id = '<session id>'; ``` 4. Observe that cumulative `tokens_cache_read` and total session tokens can grow to tens of millions even when the stored message/part JSON is only a few MB. 5. Continue the same session until the provider rejects the next request with a context-window error: ```text Your input exceeds the context window of this model. Please adjust your input and try again. ``` 6. Try enabling aggressive compaction settings such as: ```jsonc { "compaction": { "auto": true, "prune": true, "tail_turns": 1, "preserve_recent_tokens": 4000, "reserved": 12000 } } ``` The already-overflowed session still remains difficult/impossible to continue. ### Screenshot and/or share link No public share link, because the affected session contains private project data. Sanitized measurements are included above. Related existing issues that look adjacent but do not mention the `cache.read`/cumulative-session-usage aspect: - #29450 compaction loop and hitting context limit 200k on single request - #8089 Auto-compaction enabled by default, but context_length_exceeded errors still occur in agent workflows - #29857 /compact can exceed model context before summarization on large sessions - #4845 prompt is too long unrecoverable ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Terminal Windows Terminal / PowerShell

signals.title: SQLite auto_vacuum is disabled, database files grow indefinitely
signals.text: ### Describe the bug The SQLite database has `auto_vacuum = 0` (NONE) by default. Deleted rows leave behind free pages that are never reclaimed, causing the database file to grow indefinitely over time. Long-running instances accumulate significant disk usage from deleted session data, compacted messages, and old worktree snapshots. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use OpenCode for extended period with many sessions 2. Delete old sessions 3. Check database file size — it never shrinks ### Expected behavior Enable incremental auto-vacuum so free pages are reclaimed over time. Add `checkpoint()` and `vacuum()` utility functions for periodic maintenance. ### System info - OpenCode version: v1.15.3 - OS: Linux

signals.title: `opencode web` shows `ENOENT: xdg-open` error in container environments
signals.text: ## Description Running `opencode web` inside a container (Docker/Podman) without a desktop environment prints an ugly `ENOENT` error because `xdg-open` is not present in the image. The full error: ``` 662 | var file = this.spawnfile = options.file, spawnargs; 663 | if (options.args === @undefined) 664 | spawnargs = this.spawnargs = []; 665 | else 666 | validateArray(options.args, "options.args"), spawnargs = this.spawnargs = options.args; 667 | if (this.#handle = Bun.spawn({ Error: Executable not found in $PATH: "xdg-open" path: "xdg-open", errno: -2, syscall: "spawn xdg-open", code: "ENOENT" at spawn (node:child_process:667:35) at spawn (node:child_process:14:39) at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-8mgmcy90.js:3:5152) ``` ### Update (1.17.3) Since **1.17.3** the HTTP server **does start** even when `xdg-open` is missing — the crash in 1.17.1 was fixed on 1.17.3. However, the error is still printed to stderr on startup, which is noisy and confusing for users running in containers. The error has no useful meaning in a container environment: there is no desktop session, no `$DISPLAY`, and no browser to open. The server works fine, but the user sees a scary stack trace before any output. ## Root cause When `opencode web` starts, it spawns `xdg-open` to open the user's default browser. In a container environment (no desktop session, no `$DISPLAY`, no `xdg-utils` installed), this call fails with `ENOENT`. In 1.17.1 the exception killed the entire process. In 1.17.3 the crash is fixed, but the error is still logged to stderr before the server starts. The server and the browser-opening logic should be decoupled: a missing or failed browser launch should be silent (or at most a warning) in headless environments. ## Why this matters ### 1. Containers are a first-class deployment target OpenCode's own install page documents `docker run -it --rm ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode` as an official installation method. Containers are also used for: - **CI/CD pipelines** — running opencode in automated workflows - **Remote development** — SSH into a host that runs opencode in a container, access the web UI from the browser on the local machine - **Multi-tenant setups** — isolating projects in separate containers on the same host - **Development environments** — using Dev Containers, Podman, or Docker Compose for reproducible workspaces In all these scenarios, the browser runs on the *host*, not inside the container. The container should only serve the web UI; the user opens it manually from their host browser. ### 2. The web server and the browser launch are separate concerns `opencode web` serves an HTTP interface. Opening a browser is a convenience feature for local desktop usage, but it should not be a hard requirement for the server to start. In headless or containerized contexts, this convenience becomes a blocker. ### 3. No graceful fallback exists There is currently no flag like `--no-open` or `--no-browser` to skip the browser launch. The environment variable `BROWSER` is not checked. The only workaround is either: - Installing `xdg-utils` inside the container (pointless — there is no browser to open) - Creating a fake `/usr/local/bin/xdg-open` no-op script (as done in `Containerfile` in this directory) Neither is a proper solution. ## Suggested fix The browser launch error should be suppressed or downgraded to a debug-level log when `xdg-open` is not found: ```typescript try { spawn('xdg-open', [url]); } catch (err) { // Container/headless environment — not an error } ``` Additionally, consider adding: - A `--no-open` / `--no-browser` CLI flag for `opencode web` - Support for the `BROWSER` environment variable as an alternative to `xdg-open` - A `server.openBrowser` config option in `opencode.json` (default: `true`) ## Workaround (immediate) When you create a custom container and add the standard installation method: Add this to your Containerfile before the `ENTRYPOINT`: ```dockerfile # Create a fake xdg-open RUN printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > /usr/local/bin/xdg-open && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/xdg-open ``` This creates a no-op `xdg-open` that satisfies the executable check without actually trying to open a browser. ## Environment - **OpenCode version:** 1.17.1+ (error persists in 1.17.3, though the crash was fixed) - **OS:** Any Linux container (Debian, Alpine, etc.) - **Runtime:** Docker, Podman, or any OCI-compatible container runtime ### Plugins standard opencode plugin as it comes from the factory ### OpenCode version 1.17.3 but from 1.17.1 exist the issue ### Steps to reproduce Simply pull the standard image: podman pull ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode:1.17.3 and run with the web parameter and the error will be displayed on the screen. But this is my Containerfile ```dockerfile FROM docker.io/debian:stable-backports ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive ENV PIP_USER=true # Pre-configurar tshark para que no requiera setuid (ejecutamos como root en el contenedor) RUN echo "wireshark-common wireshark-common/install-setuid boolean false" | debconf-set-selections # Instalar todas las herramientas: esenciales, build, python, red y utilidades varias RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \ ca-certificates \ curl \ git \ jq \ bash \ file \ unzip \ zip \ gcc \ g++ \ make \ && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* # Crear la estructura de directorios usada por opencode.sh para XDG y PYTHONUSERBASE RUN mkdir -p /home/opencode/.config \ /home/opencode/.local/state \ /home/opencode/.local/share \ /home/opencode/.pythonuser # Instalar opencode mediante el instalador oficial RUN curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash \ && ln -sf /root/.opencode/bin/opencode /usr/local/bin/opencode # Copiar y preparar el entrypoint que decide entre modo web y TUI COPY entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/opencode-entrypoint.sh RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/opencode-entrypoint.sh # Base para paquetes Python instalados por el usuario (persistente mediante volumen) ENV PYTHONUSERBASE=/home/opencode/.pythonuser # Directorio de trabajo por defecto: coincide con el volumen montado en opencode.sh WORKDIR /workspace # Puerto por defecto del servidor web de opencode EXPOSE 4096 # Por defecto se arranca el servidor web en 0.0.0.0:4096. # El modo TUI se activa con OPENCODE_MODE=tui (lo hace opencode.sh con --tui/--no-web). ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/opencode-entrypoint.sh"] CMD ["web", "--port", "4096", "--hostname", "0.0.0.0"] ``` Entrypoint.sh ```shell #!/bin/bash set -e # opencode container entrypoint. # El modo se selecciona mediante la variable de entorno OPENCODE_MODE: # - web (por defecto): ejecuta `opencode` con los argumentos recibidos # (típicamente los del CMD: web --port N --hostname ...) # - tui: ejecuta `opencode` sin argumentos (arranca la TUI) MODE="${OPENCODE_MODE:-web}" case "$MODE" in tui) exec opencode ;; web) exec opencode "$@" ;; *) echo "[ERROR] OPENCODE_MODE desconocido: '$MODE' (valores válidos: 'web', 'tui')" >&2 exit 1 ;; esac ``` ### Screenshot and/or share link ▄ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀▄ █▀▀▀ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █ █ █ █ █▀▀▀ █ █ █ █ █ █ █ █▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ █▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ Local access: http://localhost:4097 Network access: http://192.168.0.113:4097 662 | var file = this.spawnfile = options.file, spawnargs; 663 | if (options.args === @undefined) 664 | spawnargs = this.spawnargs = []; 665 | else 666 | validateArray(options.args, "options.args"), spawnargs = this.spawnargs = options.args; 667 | if (this.#handle = Bun.spawn({ ^ error: Executable not found in $PATH: "xdg-open" path: "xdg-open", errno: -2, syscall: "spawn xdg-open", spawnargs: [ "http://localhost:4097" ], code: "ENOENT" at spawn (node:child_process:667:35) at spawn (node:child_process:14:39) at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-j1dejnx8.js:3:5152) ### Operating System Host Debian 13 , podman 5.4.2, inside the container: docker.io/debian:stable-backports ### Terminal terminator but this not matter

signals.title: fix(flock): log file-lock heartbeat failures instead of silencing
signals.text: ### Description In `packages/core/src/util/flock.ts:230`, the file lock's heartbeat timer silently swallows all filesystem errors: ```ts timer = setInterval(() => { const t = new Date() void utimes(heartbeatPath, t, t).catch(() => undefined) }, intervalMs) ``` The heartbeat is the mechanism by which the current lock holder signals it is still alive. If the heartbeat write fails (disk full, filesystem error, permissions changed, heartbeat path deleted), the error is entirely ignored. Without a functioning heartbeat: 1. Another process polling the lock may detect the lock as **stale** and steal it. 2. Both processes could then hold the lock simultaneously, leading to **concurrent writes** to the same protected resource. 3. This can cause **data corruption** in the critical sections protected by this lock. **Fix**: Log the error so it's visible: ```diff - void utimes(heartbeatPath, t, t).catch(() => undefined) + void utimes(heartbeatPath, t, t).catch((err) => console.warn("lock heartbeat failed:", err)) ``` ### Plugins n/a ### OpenCode version dev ### Steps to reproduce Cause the heartbeat filesystem path to become unwritable (e.g. permissions change, disk full) while a file lock is held. The heartbeat silently stops without warning. ### Screenshot and/or share link n/a ### Operating System n/a ### Terminal n/a

signals.title: AJV schema validation warnings (unknown format google-duration/uint64) from Google Cloud MCP servers
signals.text: ## Environment - **OpenCode version:** 1.17.7 - **OS:** Windows (win32) ## Summary When using Google Cloud remote MCP servers, OpenCode prints AJV schema validation warnings to stderr during startup. The servers and tools work correctly, but the warnings clutter output and cannot be suppressed via any config option or CLI flag. ## Observed Behavior ``` [2026-06-19T02:58:30Z WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "google-duration" ignored in schema at path "#/properties/messageRetentionDuration" in googlepubsub/tools/topics_list [2026-06-19T02:58:30Z WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "google-duration" ignored in schema at path "#/$defs/PasswordValidationPolicy/properties/passwordChangeInterval" in googlecloudsql/tools/instances_list [2026-06-19T02:58:30Z WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "google-duration" ignored in schema at path "#/properties/versionRetentionPeriod" in googlestorage/tools/buckets_list [2026-06-19T02:58:30Z WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "uint64" ignored in schema at path "#/properties/id" in googlecompute/tools/instances_list [2026-06-19T02:58:30Z WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "uint64" ignored in schema at path "#/$defs/MaterializedViewDefinition/properties/refreshIntervalMs" in googlebigquery/tools/datasets_list ``` ## Affected Servers | Server | Format | |--------|--------| | google-pubsub | google-duration | | google-cloud-sql | google-duration | | google-cloud-storage | google-duration | | google-cloud-run | google-duration | | google-monitoring | google-duration | | google-logging | google-duration | | google-maps | google-duration | | google-compute | uint64 | | google-bigquery | uint64 | ## How to Reproduce 1. Create a minimal config (`test.jsonc`): ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "mcp": { "google-pubsub": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.googleapis.com/pubsub" } } } ``` 2. Run: ``` opencode --config test.jsonc run "hello" ``` 3. Observe warnings in stderr No authentication needed — the warning fires during schema fetch before any API call. ## What Doesn't Suppress It - `--log-level ERROR` - `opencode serve` (headless mode) - Config `timeout` option - `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-warnings` - Global `"tools": { "google-*": false }` ## Expected Behavior Either: 1. Downgrade the log level from `warn` to `debug`/`trace` when AJV is configured to ignore unknown formats 2. Expose a config option to control schema validation verbosity 3. Register Google's custom format specifiers so they pass validation cleanly ## Root Cause The MCP client validates tool schemas with AJV. Google Cloud MCP servers use custom JSON Schema format keywords (`google-duration`, `uint64`) not registered with the AJV instance. AJV warns for each unknown format even when configured to ignore them. ## Workaround (fragile) ``` opencode run "<prompt>" 2>&1 | Where-Object {$_ -notmatch 'unknown format'} ```
signals.author: ThisIsSheikhRidwan

signals.title: MCP tool schemas with extended format values emit unknown format warnings
signals.text: ## Description When connecting to MCP servers that use extended JSON Schema format values beyond the JSON Schema Validation spec (e.g. `google-duration`, `uint64`, `int64`, `google-field-mask`), opencode emits warnings at startup: ``` [WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "google-duration" for key "duration" console.warn("unknown format 'uint64' will not be validated") ``` These warnings come from two sources: 1. The MCP SDK's internal AJV validator (compiling tool `outputSchema`) 2. The structured `opencode::mcp::registry` logger (processing tool `inputSchema`) ## How we got here Discovered while setting up the Google Cloud Pub/Sub MCP server. On startup, dozens of `unknown format` warnings flooded stderr — one for each tool schema property using `google-duration`, `uint64`, `int64`, `google-field-mask`, etc. Tracing backward: 1. The MCP `Client` internally creates an AJV instance with `validateFormats: true`. Non-standard formats in `outputSchema` cause `console.warn`. 2. The AI SDK's `jsonSchema()` function also encounters these non-standard formats, triggering `[WARN opencode::mcp::registry]`. Neither source is a functional bug — AJV still accepts the schema, just warns. But the noise makes startup logs hard to read. ## Expected Behavior No warnings about unknown JSON Schema format values from MCP tool schemas. Non-standard formats should be silently ignored.
signals.author: ThisIsSheikhRidwan

signals.title: Cloudflare AI Gateway (Unified Billing) rejects `role: "system"` in messages array when proxying Anthropic models — no way to suppress/remap system messages per-provider
signals.text: ### Description ## Environment - **opencode version**: 1.17.8 - **Provider config**: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` pointing to Cloudflare AI Gateway Unified Billing endpoint - **Endpoint**: `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT_ID}/ai/v1/chat/completions` - **Model**: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` - **OS**: Windows / Linux / macOS (reproduced on Windows) --- ## Problem Cloudflare AI Gateway Unified Billing routes requests to Anthropic's backend. When the model is `anthropic/*`, the gateway applies Anthropic's validation rules, which **do not accept `role: "system"` inside the `messages` array**. The system prompt must be sent as a top-level `system` field, not as a `messages[0]` entry. OpenCode injects its system prompt as `{ "role": "system", "content": "..." }` in the `messages` array (via `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` → `convertToOpenAICompatibleChatMessages`). This causes every request to fail with: ```json { "error": { "message": "Invalid value at messages[0].role: Invalid option: expected one of \"user\"|\"assistant\"", "type": "invalid_request_error" } } ``` Minimal reproduction (direct API call) Fails: ``` POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT_ID}/ai/v1/chat/completions { "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6", "messages": [ { "role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant." }, { "role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: test ok" } ] } ``` Works (system message removed): ``` { "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: test ok" } ] } ``` Note: OpenAI models on the same Cloudflare endpoint (openai/gpt-4o, etc.) accept role: "system" correctly — this is Anthropic-backend-specific behavior enforced by the gateway. ### Root cause In @ai-sdk/openai-compatible, the system role is always converted to: // convert-to-openai-compatible-chat-messages.ts ``` case 'system': { messages.push({ role: 'system', content, ...metadata }); break; } ``` OpenCode passes the system prompt through this path unconditionally. The @ai-sdk/openai-compatible package exposes a transformRequestBody callback at construction time that could intercept and rewrite messages, but OpenCode does not expose this to users (it is a function and cannot be serialised to JSON config). ### Workaround (current) The only current workaround is to run a local HTTP proxy between OpenCode and Cloudflare that strips/remaps the system message. This is unnecessarily complex for a configuration-level problem. ### Related issues - #30381 — Bad input on Cloudflare Workers AI (different cause: array/string content mismatch, but same gateway) - #31156 — stream_options injected on Databricks AI Gateway (same root pattern: OpenCode emits fields that some gateways reject; fix: per-provider opt-out flag) ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

The ideal setup would be a yaml file in which I get to specify nodes and transitions, and specify which agent description should be used for which node, and which command-line-tool or smaller agent should be run on each attempted transition, and how a transition failure should be reported back (e.g. just a descriptive error message from the command-line tool acting as gate, or a full rebuttal from a small agent acting as gate). Features could include: * Browse all supported configuration categories * View current values * Edit settings through prompts, toggles, selectors, and input fields * Validate values before saving * Display descriptions/help text for each setting * Create `opencode.json` automatically if it does not exist * Preview changes before applying them * Confirm changes before writing to disk ### Example Flow ```text /settings > Models > Providers > MCP Servers > Permissions > Appearance > Advanced Select setting → Modify value → Review changes → Confirm ``` ### Session Reload After saving: 1. Write changes to `opencode.json` 2. Gracefully restart/reload the current OpenCode session 3. Return the user to the same terminal instance This ensures configuration changes take effect immediately without requiring users to manually exit and relaunch OpenCode. ### Benefits * Better onboarding experience * Reduced configuration errors * Faster discovery of available settings * Less time spent searching documentation for valid JSON keys * More consistent and user-friendly configuration workflow * Immediate feedback through automatic session reload ### Additional Considerations * Generate the menu dynamically from the configuration schema to avoid duplication and keep the UI synchronized with supported settings. * Show default values and descriptions where available. * Warn users when a setting requires a full restart or may impact active sessions.

signals.title: [BUG] MCP tools connected but not exposed to agent
signals.text: ### Description # [BUG] MCP tools connected but not exposed to agent ## Description MCP server `pdfrag` connects successfully and exposes 6 tools via `tools/list`, but the tools do not appear in the agent's available tool list. The server is working correctly (responds to MCP protocol, tools are valid), but something in the opencode pipeline isn't passing those tools to the agent. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a custom MCP server (Python, stdio transport) 2. Register in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`: ```json "mcp": { "pdfrag": { "type": "local", "command": "/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14/bin/pdfrag-mcp" } } ``` 3. Run `opencode mcp list` → shows "connected" with green checkmark 4. Start opencode session → tools NOT available to agent ## Expected Behavior MCP tools should be available as first-class tools in the agent session after successful connection. ## Actual Behavior - Server connects successfully - `opencode mcp list` shows "connected" - MCP protocol handshake works (initialize, tools/list returns 6 valid tools) - Tools do NOT appear in agent's available tool list - Agent cannot call MCP tools ## Investigation 1. **Server works correctly**: Verified with Python MCP client - server responds to `initialize`, `tools/list`, and tool calls 2. **Server format matches working servers**: Compared with `token-optimizer` and `lean-ctx` servers - same structure, capabilities, and tool definitions 3. **No error logs**: opencode logs show no errors related to pdfrag 4. **opencode binary is compiled**: Cannot inspect source directly, but binary analysis shows MCP tool registration code exists ## Similar Issue Found similar issue on hermes-agent: [#41625](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/41625) - "MCP tools discovered but not exposed to agent in TUI mode" The suspected cause there is a race condition in the TUI startup path with a timeout that's too short for MCP discovery. ## Environment - OpenCode version: 1.17.8 - OS: macOS (darwin) - Python: 3.14 - MCP transport: stdio (local subprocess) ## Workaround Use CLI or Python direct calls: ```bash python3 pdf_rag.py query "question" ``` ## Request Please investigate why MCP tools are not being exposed to the agent despite successful connection. This may be related to: - Race condition in tool discovery (similar to hermes-agent #41625) - Tool filtering logic - Agent tool context initialization ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: Unbounded growth of the `event` table: opencode.db reaches 13GB+, mostly `message.updated.1` snapshots (no retention/compaction)
signals.text: ## Summary The local SQLite store (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`) grows **unbounded** on long-lived instances because the event-sourcing `event` table is never pruned, capped, or compacted. On two of our long-running instances it reached **~13 GB each**, filling a 22 GB volume to 97–99% and eventually producing `sqlite3.OperationalError: database or disk is full` on ordinary queries — the instance becomes effectively unusable. The actual conversation data is tiny by comparison; **>90% of the DB is the event log**, and within it a single event type (`message.updated.1`) dominates. ## Measured breakdown (real instance, 13.7 GB DB) ``` page_size=4096 page_count=3342166 total=13.69 GB freelist_count=18 dead=0.00 GB (0.0%) <- live data, VACUUM does not help ``` Per-table (`sum(length(data))`): | table | rows | size | avg/row | |---------|---------|-----------|---------| | **event** | 141,951 | **12.20 GB** | 83.9 KB | | message | 6,955 | 1.15 GB | 161 KB | | part | 27,775 | 0.07 GB | 2.4 KB | | others | — | ~0 | — | Within `event`, by `type`: | event type | rows | size | avg | |-------------------------------|--------|------------|---------| | **`message.updated.1`** | 26,463 | **11.94 GB** | **440 KB** | | `session.next.tool.success.1` | 7,843 | 0.12 GB | 14.8 KB | | `message.part.updated.1` | 52,644 | 0.10 GB | 1.8 KB | | everything else | ~55k | < 0.3 GB | — | So ~87% of the entire database is `message.updated.1` events. With ~6,955 messages there are ~3.8 `message.updated` events per message, each persisting what looks like a full message snapshot (avg 440 KB), and **all historical snapshots are retained forever**. The same pattern was observed independently on a second instance (also ~13 GB, same `event`-table dominance), so this is reproducible, not a one-off. ## Root cause (confirmed in source, `dev` branch) `packages/core/src/event/sql.ts` — the `event` table has no TTL, no row cap, no size limit, and no compaction column; it just stores every event's full `data` JSON: ```ts export const EventTable = sqliteTable("event", { id: text().$type<EventV2.ID>().primaryKey(), aggregate_id: text().notNull().references(() => EventSequenceTable.aggregate_id, { onDelete: "cascade" }), seq: integer().notNull(), type: text().notNull(), data: text({ mode: "json" }).$type<Record<string, unknown>>().notNull(), }, ...) ``` `packages/core/src/event.ts` — the **only** delete against `event` is a full-aggregate cascade, used when an entire session/aggregate is removed: ```ts function remove(aggregateID: string) { return db.transaction(() => Effect.gen(function* () { yield* db.delete(EventSequenceTable).where(eq(EventSequenceTable.aggregate_id, aggregateID)).run() yield* db.delete(EventTable).where(eq(EventTable.aggregate_id, aggregateID)).run() })).pipe(Effect.orDie) } ``` There is **no partial pruning** — nothing collapses superseded `message.updated.*` snapshots, keeps only the latest per message, caps per-aggregate history, or stores deltas. `packages/opencode/src/sync/README.md` confirms this is an intentional append-only log "for session replayability." That's a reasonable design goal, but with full-snapshot `message.updated` events and no retention it means every session's event history accumulates for the lifetime of the session, with no upper bound. `SessionCompaction.prune` does **not** address this — it trims context tokens sent to the model, not persisted `event` rows. ## Impact - Disk exhaustion on long-lived instances (containers/sandboxes/servers with persistent home dirs). - Once the volume is full, even read queries that need temp space fail with `database or disk is full`. - `VACUUM` cannot reclaim it (freelist ≈ 0%; it is all live data). The only current remediation is deleting whole sessions (cascade) or manually `DELETE FROM event ...`. ## Suggested fixes (any one would help) 1. **Compact superseded snapshots**: for snapshot-style events like `message.updated.*`, retain only the latest event per `(aggregate_id, message_id)` (or per message `seq`), deleting older ones — newer fully supersedes older. 2. **Store deltas instead of full snapshots** for `message.updated` (the README already notes `session.updated` was moved to fields-only; `message.updated` appears to still carry a full snapshot). 3. **Per-aggregate retention cap / periodic compaction** of the event log for inactive/completed sessions. ## Environment - Observed on builds in the 1.15.x–1.17.x range; root cause confirmed present on `dev` (current `latest`, 1.17.9) via the source above. - SQLite store at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. Happy to provide the full per-session breakdown or a repro script if useful.

signals.text: ### Description envirment: tools value Node v26.1.0 Shell fish, inside kitty terminal RAM 14GB + 14GB swap CPU AMD Ryzen 7 6800H description: During a ~2 hour interactive session involving many consecutive bash tool invocations (setting up a macOS KVM), the opencode process RSS grew monotonically from ~300MB to a peak of 8.6GB (reported by systemd for the parent kitty scope, opencode as dominant child). The bash subprocess group alone peaked at 468MB, and open_code.db grew to ~70MB. No OOM kill occurred only due to 14GB swap + CachyOS aggressive reclaim. Meanwhile a QEMU VM consuming 4.9GB RSS was also running on the same host, making total pressure ~13.5GB. No explicit errors in ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log (1.8MB, 10093 lines). influence: Near-OOM on a 14GB host with swap thrashing. Lighter hosts would trigger OOM kill. guess: Buffered bash tool output or tool-call history not released between invocations. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.17.8 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start a long session with heavy tool-call throughput (e.g. quickemu macOS setup) 2. Make many consecutive bash calls over ~2 hours 3. Monitor with ps aux --sort=-%mem — RSS grows monotonically ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System OS CachyOS (Arch Linux), kernel 7.0.12 LTO ### Terminal kitty

signals.title: [BUG] Zen balance does not remove free usage cap; paid users still hit 200-request/free usage limit
signals.text: ### Description Users with an active OpenCode Zen balance are still being limited as if they are free-tier users. I tested this with two separate users/accounts. One account had a Zen balance of at least $20, but both accounts still hit the same free usage cap / 200 request limit and received 429 rate-limit errors. The paid/balance-enabled account did not appear to get any higher allowance or fallback to paid Zen balance. This looks like the free usage limiter is being applied before checking whether the account has Zen balance / billing enabled. Expected behavior: * Accounts without billing/balance should be limited by the free usage cap. * Accounts with Zen balance should either: * use the paid Zen balance after the free cap is reached, or * not receive the same free-tier-only limit. * The error should make clear whether this is a free quota limit, Go usage limit, monthly spend limit, provider limit, or Zen balance issue. Actual behavior: * Both free and paid/balance-enabled users hit the same limit. * The paid account still receives HTTP 429 / `FreeUsageLimitError`. * Adding $20 balance does not appear to remove or bypass the free usage cap. Sanitized example error: ```json { "statusCode": 429, "error": { "type": "FreeUsageLimitError", "message": "Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later." } } ``` This is confusing because Zen is documented as pay-per-request after adding balance, but the account still behaves like an unpaid/free account. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.17.7 Please confirm if needed; this was observed from the client/user-agent during testing. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create or use an OpenCode Zen account with at least $20 balance. 2. Use a Zen/free model such as `deepseek-v4-flash-free` or another Zen free model. 3. Send requests until the free usage cap is reached. 4. Observe that the account still receives `FreeUsageLimitError` / HTTP 429. 5. Repeat with another user/account without balance. 6. Compare behavior: both accounts appear to receive the same 200-request/free usage cap despite one having Zen balance. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Linux container ### Terminal OpenCode CLI / server environment

signals.title: OpenCode v1.17.10 crashes with Bun segmentation fault on Windows; v1.17.9 appears stable
signals.text: ### Description ## Summary After upgrading OpenCode to `v1.17.10`, OpenCode started crashing with a native Bun segmentation fault on Windows. Downgrading to `v1.17.9` appears to stop the fatal crash under the same repository/configuration/session pattern. This looks like a possible regression in the Windows standalone executable / embedded Bun runtime rather than an application-level configuration error. ## Environment - OS: Windows 11 - OpenCode install method: npm global, via nvm4w - OpenCode version with crash: `1.17.10` - OpenCode version that appears stable: `1.17.9` - Node: `v24.11.1` - npm: `11.6.2` - Bun CLI installed globally: no - Bun shown by crash report: `Bun v1.3.14` - Architecture shown by crash report: `windows x64 (baseline)` / `windows x86_64_baseline [StandaloneExecutable]` - Runtime mode shown by crash report: `standalone_executable` ## Crash output ```text Bun v1.3.14 (0d9b296a) Windows x64 (baseline) Windows v.win11_dt CPU: sse42 avx avx2 Args: "C: vm4w odejs ode_modules\opencode-ai in\opencode.exe" "--user-agent=opencode/1.17.10" "--use-system-ca" "--" Features: Bun.stderr(4) Bun.stdin(4) Bun.stdout(4) abort_signal fetch(52) jsc spawn(772) standalone_executable workers_spawned(2) napi_module_register process_dlopen panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x2366F192AA2 oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code. ``` A second crash report from the Bun crash page showed: ```text Bun v1.3.14 (0d9b296a) on windows x86_64_baseline [StandaloneExecutable] Segmentation fault at address 0x7876BAA2 Features: spawn, standalone_executable, transpiler_cache, tsconfig, virtual_modules, workers_spawned, napi_module_register, process_dlopen, Bun.stderr, Bun.stdin, Bun.stdout, abort_signal, fetch, jsc, no_avx2 ``` ## What I was doing I was running OpenCode inside a normal project directory on Windows. The session involved a heavier workflow with: - primary agent + subagents - file reads/edits - shell/tool permission prompts - snapshots/project copy refresh - GitHub Copilot provider usage - some OpenAI fallback/small-model usage in the config The crash is native and abrupt. It does not appear as a normal OpenCode application error in `opencode.log`. ## Logs / additional observations The OpenCode log does contain provider-level errors around the same period, including: - `github-copilot` / `claude-opus-4.6` returning `Bad Request` - `github-copilot` returning `Unauthorized` in one earlier run - OpenAI fallback models returning quota/timeout/overload errors - `ProviderModelNotFoundError` in share subscriber messages However, those are normal logged application/provider errors. The fatal issue reported here is the native Bun segmentation fault, which kills the process. I also noticed an auto-update attempt around the same timeframe: ```text upgraded method=npm target=1.17.10 npm warn cleanup Failed to remove some directories EPERM: operation not permitted, unlink ... opencode-windows-x64 in\opencode.exe ``` I am not sure whether this contributed to the bad state, but the crash started after the `1.17.10` update. ## Expected behavior OpenCode should not crash natively. Provider/model errors should be reported as application errors without terminating the entire process. ## Actual behavior OpenCode exits with a Bun native segmentation fault. ## Workaround Downgrading to `opencode-ai@1.17.9` appears to avoid the fatal crash under the same environment and workflow. ```powershell npm uninstall -g opencode-ai opencode-windows-x64 npm install -g opencode-ai@1.17.9 setx OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE 1 ``` ### Plugins None. I am using a custom OpenCode configuration with agents/subagents, but no OpenCode plugins. ### OpenCode version 1.17.10, Workaround: downgrading to 1.17.9 appears stable under the same environment/workflow. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install or upgrade to OpenCode v1.17.10 on Windows via npm global / nvm4w. 2. Run opencode inside a normal project directory. 3. Start a heavier session involving a primary agent, subagents, file reads/edits, shell permission prompts, snapshots/project copy refresh, and GitHub Copilot provider usage. 4. After some activity, OpenCode exits abruptly with a native Bun segmentation fault. 5. Downgrade to opencode-ai@1.17.9 and repeat the same workflow. The fatal Bun crash no longer appears, at least so far. ### Screenshot and/or share link Attached screenshot of the terminal crash. Crash excerpt: Bun v1.3.14 (0d9b296a) Windows x64 (baseline) Windows v.win11_dt Args: "C: vm4w odejs ode_modules\opencode-ai in\opencode.exe" "--user-agent=opencode/1.17.10" "--use-system-ca" "--" panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x2366F192AA2 oh no: Bun has crashed. This indicates a bug in Bun, not your code. ### Operating System Windows 11 x64 ### Terminal Windows PowerShell 5.1 PowerShell path shown by OpenCode logs: C:\WINDOWS\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.EXE Adding a note on possible related issues GitHub suggested while creating this report: - #28121 - #27446 - #26890 This may be related to those existing Bun/Windows segmentation fault reports, but the reason I opened a new issue is that this appears to be a recent `v1.17.10` regression: the same environment/workflow crashes on `1.17.10`, while downgrading to `1.17.9` appears stable so far. The crash signature is specifically Bun `v1.3.14` embedded in the Windows standalone executable.

signals.title: OpenAI-compatible providers report zero tokens_cache_read despite upstream returning cached_tokens
signals.text: ## Description `tokens_cache_read` stays 0 for OpenAI-compatible providers (litellm proxying deepseek in my case) even when the upstream returns `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` in both streaming and non-streaming responses. Other provider adapters in the same install (anthropic, zhipu, minimax) record cache hits correctly, so this is specific to the openai-compatible path. ## Plugins None relevant to this repro. ## OpenCode version 1.17.11 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Point opencode at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that surfaces cache tokens. Confirm upstream actually returns them: ``` curl -s "$URL/v1/chat/completions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4-flash","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<long repeated prefix, ~6k tokens>"}],"max_tokens":5}' \ | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["usage"])' # {"prompt_tokens":6004,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":5888}, ...} ``` Streaming responses report the same field in the final `data:` chunk. 2. Run two prompts through opencode that share a long prefix. 3. Inspect the resulting session: ``` sqlite3 -readonly ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \ "SELECT substr(id,1,16), tokens_cache_read, tokens_cache_write FROM session ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5" ``` Expected: non-zero `tokens_cache_read`. Actual: `0`. ## Contrast Same install, other providers record cache fine: ``` zhipu/glm-5.1 397 sessions tokens_cache_read = 1,074,226,894 zhipu/glm-5.2 136 sessions tokens_cache_read = 600,508,672 minimax/MiniMax-M3 395 sessions tokens_cache_read = 126,005,095 litellm/deepseek-v4-flash 11 sessions tokens_cache_read = 0 ``` ## Related issue #30663 reports zero cache tokens for **subagent** sessions on custom baseURL providers. My case differs: the **main session** records 0, and it reproduces deterministically, not just for subagents. I walked the code path: - `packages/llm/src/protocols/openai-chat.ts` maps `cached_tokens → cacheReadInputTokens` (~line 385). - `packages/llm/src/protocols/openai-compatible-chat.ts` reuses `OpenAIChat.protocol`. - `packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts` reads `usage.cacheReadInputTokens`. The mapping exists end to end, yet the value is lost somewhere between `mapUsage` and the session write. I did not pin the exact line where `cacheReadInputTokens` drops for the openai-compatible route, but the symptom is isolated to it. ## Impact Any OpenAI-compatible provider (litellm, openrouter, vLLM, Ollama compat, LM Studio) silently loses cache accounting. Cost tables and any resume/caching savings measurement against those providers are wrong by the cache fraction. ## Operating System Linux 6.1.0-40-amd64 (Debian) ## Terminal tmux 3.3a

signals.title: Google Gemini 400 schema error when function call has nullable union types
signals.text: When using Google Gemini models with function calling, Effect Schema nullable unions like ["object", "null"] generate tool schemas with type arrays. The schema sanitizer normalizes this into anyOf and removes type, but leaves required behind - which Google's API forbids on non-object types. Fix: strip required (and properties) when type is absent after normalization. ## Impact - Any Google Gemini model with function calling using nullable types - 400 Bad Request: "GenerateContentRequest.tools[0].function_declarations[...].parameters.any_of[...].required: only allowed for OBJECT type" ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure an opencode agent with a tool that has nullable parameters 2. Run: opencode run -m google/gemini-2.5-flash 3. Observe 400 error from Google API

signals.title: Custom tools from tools/ directory fail with Bun minified runtime error after first call
signals.text: ## opencode tools/ directory custom tool execution failure ### Environment - **opencode**: 1.17.13 - **Bun**: 1.3.14 - **macOS**: 26.5.1 (Sequoia) - **@opencode-ai/plugin**: 1.17.13 ### Symptom All `.ts` files in `~/.config/opencode/tools/` fail on execution with a Bun minified runtime error: ``` w0(()=>X(Q)).then is not a function. (In 'w0(()=>X(Q)).then((J)=>Y(I(J)),(J)=>Y(PX(J)))', 'w0(()=>X(Q)).then' is undefined) ``` This affects all three custom tools (`recall.ts`, `remember.ts`, `memory-stats.ts`). ### Files involved `~/.config/opencode/tools/remember.ts`: ```ts import { tool } from "@opencode-ai/plugin" export default tool({ description: "Store knowledge into knowledge.db.", args: { fact: tool.schema.string().describe("The knowledge to store"), type: tool.schema.string().default("fact"), }, async execute(args, context) { const script = process.env.HOME + "/.drewgent/scripts/ingest_fact.py" const input = JSON.stringify({ fact: args.fact, type: args.type }) const proc = Bun.spawnSync(["python3", script, "--json", input]) return proc.stdout.toString().trim() }, }) ``` ### Things tested (all fail identically) | Approach | File | Error | |----------|------|-------| | `async execute` + `Bun.$\`python3 ${script}\`.text()` | `recall.ts` (copied from known working version) | ❌ | | `async execute` + `Bun.spawnSync([...])` | `remember.ts` | ❌ | | Sync `execute` returning string | `remember.ts` | ❌ | | `execute(args, context)` with ToolContext | `remember.ts` (v1.17.13 API) | ❌ | | `await Bun.$\`...\`.text()` without pipe | `recall.ts` (same as earlier working session) | ❌ | ### What DOES work - Python scripts called directly from bash (`python3 scripts/ingest_fact.py --json '{"test":1}'`) - `bun -e` with `import { tool } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"` (plugin loads fine in isolation) - The `@opencode-ai/plugin` package is correctly installed and `tool()` factory returns a valid object ### Timing / Session behavior - Tools returned correct data **once** at the very beginning of an interactive session (session start auto-call to `recall()`) - After the initial successful call, **all** tool calls fail with the same minified error - Persists after `launchctl kickstart` of the headless `opencode serve` process (port 8642) - Plugin was already updated from 1.4.10 → 1.17.13 to match opencode version — no change ### Hypothesis The tools `tools/` auto-discovery mechanism in opencode 1.17.13 appears to have a compilation/caching issue. The first successful call suggests the tool compiles once, but subsequent invocations hit a Bun runtime issue in the generated/minified wrapper code. The error originates from Bun's internal minified function `w0()`, suggesting the issue is in how opencode wraps the tool execution callback.
