signals.title: V2 AI package: audit and close critical protocol correctness gaps
signals.text: ## Summary Track correctness and parity gaps in the V2 native `@opencode-ai/ai` package by wire protocol. This is **not** a feature wishlist. It excludes citations, provider-hosted tools, and unsupported optional capabilities. Scope is critical flow integrity: normalization, ordering, streamed-state settlement, persistence/replay, request intent, terminal outcomes, transport classification, and accounting. ## Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`) ### P0 — tool/result integrity - [x] **Coalesce parallel tool results into the immediately following user turn.** V2 previously lowered `assistant[tool_use A, tool_use B]` into `user[result A]`, `user[result B]`. Completed in #41948. - [x] **Settle or fail pending streamed tool calls at `message_stop`.** Completed in #43136. ### P0 — output and continuation integrity - [ ] **Preserve Anthropic compaction blocks and deltas.** Native accepts unknown block types structurally but silently drops compaction content from output and persisted history. - [ ] **Map compaction stop reasons and retain continuation state** rather than converting them to `unknown`. ### P1 — request normalization - [ ] **Normalize thinking budgets and answer-token semantics.** Enforce minimum budget and `budget < max_tokens`; account for thinking tokens when canonical `maxTokens` represents answer budget. - [x] **Do not silently downgrade supported system updates into wrapped user text.** Completed in #43180. - [ ] **Never replay unsigned visible `thinking` blocks.** Replay valid signed/redacted Anthropic state or fail/lower locally. - [ ] **Trim/normalize final assistant prefill whitespace** where Anthropic requires it. - [ ] **Reject, serialize, or explicitly warn for every accepted provider option.** Open-ended options currently type-check while lowering reads only `thinking` and `effort`; parallel-tool controls and request metadata can silently vanish. ### P1 — stream and accounting integrity - [ ] **Validate lifecycle ordering:** require `message_start`, reject duplicate/out-of-order starts, reject events after terminal completion, and settle open fragments at EOF. - [ ] **Aggregate raw usage once at terminal completion**, including split start/delta counters and compaction/advisor/fallback iterations. Existing tracker: #40713. - [ ] **Retain response identity and stop diagnostics:** actual served model, response ID, initial content snapshot, stop/refusal details, and complete provider metadata. ## Bedrock Converse ### P0 — tool/result integrity - [ ] **Coalesce parallel tool results into one immediately following Bedrock user turn.** Same deterministic failure class as Anthropic Messages; existing report: #41445. - [ ] **Normalize adjacent user/tool messages generally** so synthetic, compaction, and ordinary user content cannot violate Converse role/turn requirements. ### P1 — replay safety - [ ] **Keep Bedrock/Anthropic thought and tool metadata bound to compatible route origin.** Do not replay incompatible Anthropic signatures or foreign protocol state after model/provider switches. Related: #34996 and #35827. ## OpenAI Chat Completions (`/v1/chat/completions`) ### P0 — output integrity - [ ] **Preserve streamed `delta.refusal`.** Native accepts the field structurally but ignores it, allowing a refusal to become an empty successful response and disappear from persisted history. ### P0 — tool integrity - [ ] **Classify and retain truncated tool arguments correctly.** Distinguish provider truncation, transport interruption, and adapter premature finalization; never execute malformed input; add bounded safe recovery. Existing report: #36766. ### P1 — stream integrity - [ ] **Require valid terminal lifecycle state** rather than treating partial content/tool buffers as clean completion. ## OpenAI Responses (`/v1/responses`) ### P0 — tool integrity - [ ] **Finalize or fail pending function calls when `response.completed` arrives without `response.output_item.done`.** Current behavior can leave a tool permanently pending. Existing deterministic report: #37159. - [ ] **Retain terminal provider diagnostics for truncated argument buffers**, including whether the stream ended normally, finish state, and bounded byte counts. Related: #36766. ### P0 — output integrity - [ ] **Preserve `response.refusal.delta` and `response.refusal.done`.** Native ignores them, yields an empty successful response, and cannot replay the refusal. - [ ] **Do not mark reasoning-only output with no text/refusal/tool call as successful.** Existing production report: #37372. ### P1 — reasoning lifecycle - [ ] **Normalize overlapping reasoning fragments** instead of crashing the execution as `unknown`. Existing report: #36892. - [ ] **Finalize or explicitly interrupt every open reasoning/text fragment before response completion.** ## Gemini `generateContent` ### P0 — function-call integrity - [ ] **Support official incremental function arguments (`partialArgs` / `willContinue`).** Native currently requires complete `name + args` in each frame, so valid Gemini streams fail schema decoding before accumulation. - [x] **Normalize omitted zero-argument call input to `{}`.** A valid `functionCall: { name: "ping" }` currently fails decoding. Completed in #43111. ### P0 — safety outcome integrity - [x] **Preserve prompt-level safety blocks (`promptFeedback.blockReason`) as a typed terminal outcome.** Candidate-less blocked prompts currently lose the safety reason and become generic incomplete-stream failures. Completed in #43070. ## Shared V2 runner/history layer ### P0 — successful execution contract - [ ] **A successful execution must contain usable text, a refusal, or completed tool work.** Token usage or a provider `stop` alone is insufficient. Existing report: #37372. - [ ] **Every announced local tool call must settle exactly once before its owning step terminates.** ### P1 — persistence and replay - [ ] **Bind opaque provider metadata to resolved protocol origin**, not only the configured provider/model reference. Existing trackers: #34996 and #35827. - [ ] **Distinguish normally ended fragments from cleanup-interrupted text, reasoning, and tool input.** Existing tracker: #36874. - [ ] **Do not persist interrupted raw tool input as an executable call.** ### P1 — request intent - [ ] **Keep variants effective after native package overrides.** Confirmed end-to-end: `#low`, `#high`, and `#max` for `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` through native Anthropic produced identical request bodies with no effort/thinking field. - [ ] **Every accepted request option must be serialized, explicitly ignored with a warning, or rejected locally.** ### P1 — transport and error classification - [ ] **Classify response-body resets as transport failures, not invalid model output**, and retain a sanitized low-level cause. Existing report: #39326. - [ ] **Before output starts, preserve bounded transport retry behavior.** After output/tool side effects begin, expose an explicit interrupted-step recovery path rather than silently retrying. - [ ] **Keep child-session stream failures visible to the parent** so dropped subagent work can be restarted. ## Protocol conformance matrix Add fixtures and differential tests for every native protocol covering: 1. Single, sequential, and parallel tool calls. 2. Adjacent user/tool/synthetic/system messages. 3. Missing, duplicate, reordered, and truncated stream boundaries. 4. Pending tools/fragments at every terminal event. 5. Text, refusal, safety block, content filter, empty response, and normal stop outcomes. 6. Same-origin replay and incompatible provider/model/protocol switching. 7. Request options and model variants at the actual wire body/header boundary. 8. Split streaming usage, cache counters, executor iterations, and fallback accounting. 9. Transport reset before output, during reasoning/text, during tool input, and after tool execution. ## Suggested implementation order 1. Anthropic Messages and Bedrock parallel-result normalization. 2. Pending tool settlement across Anthropic, Responses, Chat, and Gemini. 3. Refusal, safety, and empty-success outcome invariants. 4. Replay provenance and interrupted-fragment semantics. 5. Request option/variant normalization. 6. Transport classification and usage aggregation.

signals.title: service: restart leaves stale daemon and duplicated MCP servers running
signals.text: ## Summary `opencode2 service restart` starts a new `serve --service` daemon without terminating the old one; the stale daemon and its MCP server children keep running, duplicating MCP servers and leaking ~1.5 GB of RAM until manually killed. ## Environment - opencode version: 0.0.0-next-17403 (next channel, V2 beta) - OS: macOS 26.6.1 (Darwin 25.6.0, arm64) - Terminal: Apple_Terminal, TERM=xterm-256color - Shell: /bin/zsh - Install/channel: local binary in ~/.opencode/bin, channel `next` - Active plugins: ~/.config/opencode/plugins.v2/memory.ts (opencode-memory) ## Reproduction 1. Configure local MCP servers (e.g. `npx -y @playwright/mcp --browser chromium` and `npx -y @llmindset/hf-mcp-server`) in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. 2. Start a session (spawns the `serve --service` daemon plus the MCP children). 3. Run `opencode2 service restart` (or `service stop` followed by starting a new session). 4. Inspect the process tree: the old daemon and its MCP children are still alive next to the new daemon and its own fresh MCP children. Observed today on macOS arm64: - Old daemon PID 79746 `opencode2 serve --service`, RSS ~700-780 MB, still running after the restart - Its children still alive: 2x `npm exec @playwright/mcp --browser chromium` and 1x `npm exec @llmindset/hf-mcp-server`, ~85-90 MB each - New daemon PID 80086 with its own set of MCP servers - Net result: two Playwright MCP instances running concurrently, ~1.5 GB held by the stale tree ## Expected Behavior `service restart` (and `service stop`) should terminate the previous daemon's entire process tree, including its MCP children, before starting the new one. ## Actual Behavior The old daemon and all its MCP children keep running after the restart, duplicating MCP servers and leaking memory. The stale tree could only be cleaned manually (`kill -9` on the old daemon), and it took its MCP children down with it. ## Additional Context Combined with the daemon's high idle RSS (see related perf issue), opencode2 processes peaked at ~2 GB RSS on a 16 GB MacBook Air. The duplication happened on a single restart, so it looks consistent rather than intermittent. Related: an earlier service restart had also left the previous daemon's MCP servers behind, which is how multiple Playwright instances accumulated.
signals.author: cioffiAI

signals.title: Same git remote URL produces identical project_id for different local clones → only one project visible in desktop sidebar
signals.text: ### Description # Title (EN) Same git remote URL produces identical project_id for different local clones → only one project visible in desktop sidebar # 标题 (中文) 相同的 git remote URL 导致不同本地 clone 生成相同的 project_id，桌面端侧边栏只能看到一个项目 --- ## English version ### Description When two local directories are clones of the **same git remote** (but on different branches / versions), opencode assigns them the **same `project_id`**. As a result, the desktop client aggregates them into a single entry in the sidebar project list, and only the first-added project is usable. The second directory cannot be added/switched to as a separate project. ### Environment - opencode desktop: 1.18.18 (Windows) - OS: Windows ### Reproduction steps 1. Clone the same repo into two local directories, e.g.: - `/path/to/repo-branchA` (branch A) - `/path/to/repo-branchB` (branch B) 2. Both have the same remote origin URL: ``` origin https://git.example.com/group/repo.git ``` 3. Add both directories as projects in the desktop client. 4. Observe the sidebar: only **one** project entry is shown. ### Expected behavior Both directories should be listed as separate projects (or at least be switchable), since they are different working directories with different branches. ### Actual behavior Both directories resolve to the same `project_id`: ``` <sha1 hash> ``` which is `sha1("git-remote:git.example.com/group/repo")`. The desktop sidebar deduplicates by `project_id`, so only the first-added project is visible. ### Root cause (from source inspection) In `Project.resolve` (`node-4IhTfWZ9.js` around line 85716), the `project_id` is resolved with this priority: 1. `sha1("git-remote:" + normalizedRemoteUrl)` ← **always wins when a remote is set** 2. cached value in `.git/opencode` 3. root commit hash (`git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD`) Since both clones share the same remote URL, step 1 produces an identical id, and the fallbacks are never reached. Even the root-commit fallback would be identical here because both clones share the same root commit. The `project_directory` table already supports a many-to-one mapping (PK is `(project_id, directory)`), so the **data layer** can hold multiple directories per project. The limitation is in the **UI**, which aggregates by `project_id` only. ### Why this matters For developers who maintain multiple versions/branches of the same repo side-by-side (e.g. a maintenance branch + a development branch), this makes it impossible to manage them as separate projects in the desktop client. ### Suggested improvements (any of) 1. **UI**: Show distinct entries per `directory` even when they share a `project_id` (the `project_directory` table already supports this). 2. **ID resolution**: Incorporate the local working directory (or branch) into the `project_id` as a tiebreaker when remote URLs collide, e.g. `sha1("git-remote:" + remote + ":" + worktreePath)` or `sha1(remote + "@" + branch)`. 3. **Workspace**: Allow registering an existing independent clone directory as a workspace target (currently workspaces only support `git worktree`-linked directories). --- ## 中文版 ### 问题描述 当两个本地目录是**同一个 git remote** 的 clone（但分支/版本不同）时，opencode 会给它们分配**相同的 `project_id`**。这导致桌面端在侧边栏的项目列表里把两者聚合成一条，只能看到最先添加的那个项目，第二个目录无法作为独立项目添加/切换使用。 ### 环境信息 - opencode 桌面端：1.18.18（Windows） - 操作系统：Windows ### 复现步骤 1. 把同一个仓库 clone 到两个本地目录，例如： - `/path/to/repo-branchA`（分支 A） - `/path/to/repo-branchB`（分支 B） 2. 两者的 remote origin URL 相同： ``` origin https://git.example.com/group/repo.git ``` 3. 在桌面端把这两个目录都添加为项目。 4. 观察侧边栏：只显示了**一个**项目条目。 ### 期望行为 两个目录应作为独立项目展示（或至少可切换），因为它们是不同的工作目录、不同分支。 ### 实际行为 两个目录解析出了相同的 `project_id`： ``` <sha1 hash> ``` 即 `sha1("git-remote:git.example.com/group/repo")`。 桌面端侧边栏按 `project_id` 去重，因此只显示最先添加的项目。 ### 根因（源码分析） 在 `Project.resolve`（`node-4IhTfWZ9.js` 约 85716 行）中，`project_id` 按以下优先级解析： 1. `sha1("git-remote:" + 规范化后的 remote URL)` ← **只要设置了 remote 就一定命中** 2. `.git/opencode` 缓存文件 3. root commit hash（`git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD`） 由于两个 clone 的 remote URL 相同，第 1 步就产生相同 id，fallback 永远不会触发。即便走到 fallback，root commit 也相同（同源仓库），结果仍会一致。 `project_directory` 表本身已支持多目录映射（主键是 `(project_id, directory)` 联合主键），**数据层**可以容纳同一 project_id 下的多个目录。限制在 **UI 层**——只按 `project_id` 聚合展示。 ### 为什么这很重要 对于需要并行维护同一仓库多个版本/分支的开发者（例如同时维护某个维护分支和开发另一个分支），这导致无法在桌面端把它们作为独立项目来管理。 ### 建议改进（任选其一） 1. **UI**：即使 `project_id` 相同，也按 `directory` 展示不同条目（`project_directory` 表已支持）。 2. **ID 解析**：当 remote URL 冲突时，把本地工作目录（或分支）纳入 `project_id` 计算，例如 `sha1("git-remote:" + remote + ":" + worktreePath)` 或 `sha1(remote + "@" + branch)`。 3. **Workspace**：允许把已有的独立 clone 目录注册为 workspace 目标（目前 workspace 只支持 `git worktree` 关联的目录）。 ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: Multi-step tool calls overwrite token counts instead of accumulating (output, reasoning, cache.write lost)
signals.text: ## Bug In multi-step tool-call assistant messages, `processor.ts` overwrites `assistantMessage.tokens` on each `step-finish` event instead of accumulating additive fields. Only the last step's output, reasoning, and cache.write survive. ## Root cause `packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts` step-finish handler: ```ts ctx.assistantMessage.cost += usage.cost // accumulates ctx.assistantMessage.tokens = usage.tokens // overwrites! ``` ## Impact For an assistant message with N tool-call steps, the message-level tokens only reflect the last step: - Context metrics (session context meter) under-report token usage for multi-step messages - `compaction.isOverflow` checks use `lastFinished.tokens` (`prompt.ts`), so underestimating tokens delays auto-compaction and makes the next request more likely to hit the provider context limit ## Notes - Follow-up to #21913, which was auto-closed for inactivity (bot comment says to open a new one if still relevant). The bug still exists on the latest `dev`. - Earlier fix attempts (#22077, #22032, #10215) were closed unmerged by automated cleanup, not by technical review. ## Expected behavior Output, reasoning, and cache.write tokens should accumulate across steps (like `cost` already does). Input and cache.read should keep the final step's values, since the final step's request already includes all prior steps.

signals.title: Compaction request exceeds context window on high-output models (v2)
signals.text: ### Description A V2 session using a custom OpenAI-compatible model reached about 236k of its 299,964-token context window (79%). Automatic compaction did not run, and `/compact` failed because the provider reported that the prompt plus requested output exceeded the context limit. The model advertises a 131,072-token output limit. `SessionCompaction.required()` caps its reserved output budget at 32,000, but the compaction `LLM.request()` does not set `generation.maxTokens`. OpenAI-compatible lowering therefore leaves `max_tokens` unset, allowing the provider to use 131,072 instead. Expected: the compaction request should use the same bounded output budget used to calculate the automatic-compaction threshold. Before `/compact`, the model also returned `finish=stop` with no text or tool calls several times, leaving the TUI with no visible response. This may be a separate empty-response issue. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 0.0.0-next-17403 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a custom OpenAI-compatible model with context limit 299964 and output limit 131072. 2. Grow a V2 session to approximately 236k tokens, displayed as 79% context usage. 3. Observe that automatic compaction does not run. 4. Run `/compact`. 5. Observe that the provider rejects the request because the prompt plus requested output exceeds the context window. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: Deleting a session is slow/hangs, leaves ghost sessions, and can freeze the whole app
signals.text: ### Description Deleting a session in the desktop app is very slow, often hangs, and can freeze the entire app — with no error output in the logs. All three symptoms below appear to share one root cause: session removal (`removing share`) gets stuck. Observed symptoms (opencode 1.18.18 desktop, Windows 10): 1. **Deletion is slow / hangs.** A single deletion takes 10–30+ seconds; the UI becomes unresponsive. In the log (`%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opencode\log\opencode.log`) consecutive `removing share` entries during a bulk delete of ~40 sessions show gaps of 6–28 seconds each. 2. **Ghost sessions.** If the app is killed during a deletion, the deleted session still appears on the home screen after restart. Clicking it opens the chat and immediately errors instead of loading. The interrupted removal apparently leaves the session in the local DB. 3. **Full freeze, silent.** The app sometimes stops logging entirely and must be force-killed. Three incidents today (local time): - 11:50 → 12:11 (21.8 min of silence) right after the bulk deletion above; - 16:02 → 16:17 (14.6 min, no graceful shutdown) right after opening/closing a terminal (`creating session` pty → `removing session`); - 16:26:31 (`exiting loop`) → 16:27:54 (`removing share`) → hung until killed at ~16:28:25. A normal shutdown logs `disposing all instances`; in the 16:02 incident that never appeared. No `level=ERROR`, no stack trace, no abort — pure silent hang. ### Plugins None (only the default `@opencode-ai/plugin` dependency in `~/.config/opencode/package.json`; no custom plugins or config) ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 (desktop app) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Delete a session from the home screen (single or multiple) 2. Observe that deletion takes tens of seconds or hangs the UI 3. If the app freezes, force-kill it and restart 4. The "deleted" session still appears on the home screen 5. Click that session → an error occurs instead of loading the chat 6. Optionally: open and close a terminal to reproduce the silent freeze ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Win11 ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: service (v2): serve --service daemon keeps using old OPENCODE_API_KEY after the key is rotated (401 with no hint)
signals.text: ## Summary After rotating my `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, `opencode2` kept failing with `Provider request failed with HTTP 401: Invalid API key` — from fresh shells, even though the new key was valid. The cause: a background `opencode2 serve --service` process started days earlier (before the rotation) was still holding the old key in its environment, and all CLI requests routed through that stale server. Killing the daemon fixed it immediately. ## Environment - opencode version: 0.0.0-next-17403 (next channel, v2 beta) - OS: macOS (Darwin, arm64) - Install: local binary in ~/.opencode/bin - Credential: `OPENCODE_API_KEY` set via env var in shell profile ## Reproduction 1. Start `opencode2 serve --service` (or just start a session) with a valid `OPENCODE_API_KEY`. 2. Rotate the key: change `OPENCODE_API_KEY` in the environment for new shells. 3. Open a fresh shell and run `opencode2 run "hi"`. ## Actual result ``` Error: Provider request failed with HTTP 401: Invalid API key. ``` The error gives no indication that the running server process was started with a different (now-revoked) key. I confirmed the new key was valid by calling the provider endpoint directly (`curl` with the new key returns 200). `ps` showed the daemon had been running since before the rotation. ## Expected result Some signal that the running `serve --service` daemon may hold an outdated credential — e.g. the 401 error mentioning the running server process — would have made this a 30-second fix instead of a debugging session. Restarting the daemon (`kill` + rerun) resolves it. Possibly related to the daemon-lifecycle issues #37239 and #42270.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Add Qwen3.8-27B
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request Requesting the inclusion of the Qwen3.8-27B open-weight model in the OpenCode Go subscription catalog (opencode-go/...). Adding this mid-sized model will give users a high-performing, cost-efficient option for everyday coding tasks, local-agent parity, and fast multi-file refactoring within the OpenCode ecosystem. Proposed Solution Integrate Qwen3.8-27B into the OpenCode Go managed model catalog. Expose the endpoint under the explicit runtime reference (e.g., opencode-go/qwen3.8-27b). Provide standard OpenAI/Anthropic API compatibility for seamless integration with the OpenCode CLI, IDE extensions, and third-party coding agents. Key Reasons & Benefits - Optimal Sweet Spot for Speed & Accuracy At 27 billion parameters, Qwen3.8-27B strikes an ideal balance between low latency and strong reasoning/code-generation capabilities. It outperforms smaller 7B/14B models on complex coding benchmarks while remaining significantly faster and cheaper to serve than dense 70B+ models. - Strong Agentic & Multi-File Capabilities The Qwen series is natively tuned for tool calling, precise repository context understanding, and file editing. Adding Qwen3.8-27B directly enhances OpenCode's agentic workflows (e.g., automated refactoring, test generation, and terminal command execution). - Diversity in Open-Source Model Options Users who prefer the Qwen architecture for specific languages, long context retention, or regional strengths currently lack a mid-weight Qwen option in OpenCode Go. Adding Qwen3.8-27B fills a key gap between ultra-light models and massive, heavy-tier models.
signals.author: yapnel

signals.title: [BUG]: message.updated.1 re-serializes summary.diffs on every update, making event writes quadratic in diff size
signals.text: ### Description `message.updated.1` carries a complete message snapshot, and for user messages that snapshot includes `info.summary.diffs` — the full per-file diff list with patch text. Because a snapshot is written on every update to the message, the bytes written for one message grow as O(updates x final diff size). This is a distinct contributor from the accumulated-streaming-text growth already tracked in #33356 and #41175. Those describe assistant messages growing as streamed text accumulates. This is a *derived* field on *user* messages, recomputed and reattached wholesale on each pass, and it produces the largest individual events on the box. **Measured on a 51.3 GB `opencode.db`** (~10-14 concurrent processes, one shared file): | table | rows | data | | --- | --- | --- | | `event` | 3,103,138 | 43.96 GB | | `part` | 1,251,684 | 3.0 GB | | `message` | 309,718 | 1.7 GB | Average payload by event type, sampled over the newest 50,000 rows: | type | n | avg bytes | max bytes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `message.updated.1` | 17,249 | **40,634** | **9,662,239** | | `message.part.updated.1` | 28,043 | 1,323 | 724,969 | | `session.updated.1` | 4,674 | 698 | 4,776 | Composition of the largest observed event (13.8 MB): ``` sessionID: 32 bytes info: 13,790,816 bytes id, sessionID, role, time, agent, model ~180 bytes total summary: 13,790,560 bytes diffs: 13,790,549 bytes <- 99.996% of the event ``` `summary.diffs` was 389 entries of `{file, patch, additions, deletions, status}`, individual patches up to 1.1 MB. **The quadratic part.** Grouping `message.updated.1` by `info.id`: | message | update events | total bytes written | peak snapshot | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `msg_f7ba67…` | 236 | **1,953 MB** | 9 MB | | `msg_ff59bd…` | 156 | **1,842 MB** | 13 MB | | `msg_f6a79f…` | 222 | **1,687 MB** | 8 MB | One message whose final state is 9 MB wrote roughly 2 GB of event rows. Worst single session: 65,437 events / 17.33 GB against 401 MB of durable state — **41x amplification**, and 39.4% of all event bytes from 0.5% of event rows. **Why it becomes a hard failure rather than only disk use.** A multi-megabyte row write holds the WAL write lock long enough to push concurrent processes past `busy_timeout` (5000 ms, set in `packages/core/src/database/database.ts`). An independent report on the same box captured a turn dying with `Failed to execute statement` *after* a 7.1 MB provider response had streamed successfully — tokens spent, persistence lost — inside a 900 ms window where three other processes logged `database is locked`. ### Source `packages/opencode/src/session/summary.ts` assigns the recomputed array back onto the message summary and updates the message: ```ts target.info.summary = { ...target.info.summary, diffs: msgDiffs } yield* sessions.updateMessage(target.info) ``` `updateMessage` publishes `MessageUpdated` with the whole `info` (`packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts`), so every diff recomputation re-serializes every patch. ### Suggested fix Diffs are derived state — recomputable from snapshots via `snapshot.diffFull`. They do not need to travel through the event bus. Storing them in a side table keyed by message id, keeping counts (`additions`/`deletions`/`files`) on the summary, and publishing a thin `{ sessionID, messageID }` notification that clients use to fetch on demand, takes the average `message.updated.1` payload from ~41 KB to ~1-2 KB without changing what any consumer can render. Note for anyone attempting this: four client sites read `summary.diffs` off the delivered message object rather than refetching (`packages/app/src/pages/session/timeline/rows.ts`, `packages/app/src/pages/session.tsx`, `packages/session-ui/src/components/session-turn.tsx`, `packages/session-ui/src/components/message-nav.tsx`). Removing the payload without a client fetch path blanks all four, and it fails silently — the timeline gates on `diffs.length > 0`, so the row simply stops appearing. ### OpenCode version 1.18.15
signals.author: iceteaSA

signals.title: [BUG]: (Incorrect) sampling parameters are hard-coded based on model name/id
signals.text: ### Description opencode automatically adds sampling parameters to chat requests for some model names/ids, even if not configured to do so. I think that opencode should not be doing this, or there should be a way to opt-out, or it should be changed to an opt-in setting. The defaults are defined in: ```text packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts ``` Specifically: - `ProviderTransform.temperature()` - `ProviderTransform.topP()` - `ProviderTransform.topK()` They are applied in: ```text packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts ``` The checks use substring matches against the model name/id (lowercased) Current defaults include: - Model IDs containing `north-mini-code`: temperature `1.0` - Model IDs containing `qwen`: temperature `0.55`, top_p `1.0` - Matching Gemini 2.5, Gemini 3 Flash/Pro, Gemini 3.1, and Gemini 3.5 Flash models: temperature `1.0`, top_p `0.95`, top_k `64` - Model IDs containing `glm-4.6` or `glm-4.7`: temperature `1.0` - Model IDs containing `minimax-m2`: temperature `1.0`, top_p `0.95`, top_k `20` or `40` - Model IDs containing `kimi-k2`: temperature `0.6` or `1.0` - Kimi K2.5 variants: top_p `0.95` - DeepSeek V4 Flash models: top_p `0.95` in specific cases I discovered this when running Qwen 3.8 27B locally in llama.cpp and pointing my opencode config at it. The recommended setting for Qwen 3.8 is top-p 0.95, which is being overridden by these automatically generated sampling parameters. (I specify temperature and top-p settings in llama.cpp for the model) This means i need to also set top_p in opencode config to work around this hardcoded value. ### Plugins none ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a single local OpenAI-compatible Qwen model: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "provider": { "llama": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "options": { "baseURL": "http://localhost:8001/v1" }, "models": { "Qwen-3.8-27B": { "name": "Qwen-3.8-27B" } } } } } ``` 2. Select `Qwen-3.8-27B`. 3. Send a prompt to the model. 4. Inspect the request sent to the server. signals.title: TUI: streaming Markdown list items render with truncated content while raw is intact
signals.text: ### Description While the assistant is streaming a Markdown response, list-item contents get silently truncated in the TUI. The raw message stored in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (`part` table) is complete; only the rendered output is broken. Adjacent paragraphs render fine. - No `Code highlighting failed, falling back to plain text` warning ever prints. The opencode process's fd 2 was verified redirected to `tee` and the resulting log stayed 0 bytes for the whole session. - No exception in `opencode.log` either. - Related but distinct: #38475 reports the same silent Markdown breakage class for fenced JSON code blocks. This one is list items with a mix of `**bold**` and `` `inline code` ``. **Raw markdown (from DB, verbatim):** ```` インストール完了です。 ## 修正内容 **`runCommand` を exec チャネル（PTY なし）ベースに書き直しました。** - 以前は **PTY+shell チャネル**で `herdr pane list` を送り、プロンプトの終端を推測していたため、出力が確定せずハングしていました - 今回は **exec チャネル**（`SSHChannelRequestEvent.ExecRequest`）でコマンドを実行するので、コマンド完了でチャネルが閉じ、出力が確実に確定します - `runCommandOnConnection`（接続中の監視用）も同じ exec チャネル方式 これで、接続ボタン → herdr 一覧取得 → シート表示（または通常接続）が確実に動くはずです。 ## 確認 1. 接続ボタンを押す → スピナー → herdr セッションのシートが出る、または通常接続される 2. 通常接続が復活したか 動作確認して、結果を教えてください。 ```` **Rendered in TUI (see screenshot):** - `- 以前` — everything after `以前` dropped - `- 今回は exec チャネル (` `` ` `` — truncated at the opening backtick - `- ` `` ` `` — only the opening backtick, rest dropped - `1. 接続ボタンを` — rest dropped - `2. 通常` — rest dropped The two paragraphs and the H2 headings render fully. The bold+inline-code header line (`**\`runCommand\` を exec ...`) renders fully. The `これで、接続ボタン → herdr ...` paragraph after the bullet list also renders fully. ### Investigation notes - Marked's lexer parses the same raw text into complete tokens (each list item's inline `text` / `strong` / `codespan` sequence is intact). - Chunked-feed simulation (5 chars/chunk) into `MarkdownRenderable` with `streaming: true` — tried with both `MockTreeSitterClient` and the real markdown `TreeSitterClient`. Final rendered frame contains full content in both cases. Not reproducible outside the production binary this way. - Likely path: `CodeRenderable` used for list-item text keeps its `textBuffer` at the `initialStyledText` snapshot (built at item-construction time from the inline tokens at that moment). Under real streaming timing where the highlight loop is repeatedly preempted before it can `setStyledText`, the buffer never advances. ### Plugins None. ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 ### Steps to reproduce Not reliably reproducible on demand. Happens sporadically while the assistant streams a Markdown response that contains list items mixing `**bold**` and `` `inline code` ``. The example above was captured mid-session in a long-running build task. ### Screenshot and/or share link ### Operating System macOS 26.3.1 (Darwin 25.3.0), Apple Silicon. ### Terminal herdr (terminal multiplexer), running inside iTerm 2.

signals.title: OpenCode Go quota exhausted in ~20 minutes after DeepSeek V4 Flash cache reads suddenly dropped to 0
signals.text: ### Description I experienced what appears to be a severe caching/billing issue with **OpenCode Go + `deepseek-v4-flash`** on August 16, 2026. My Go usage was around **11% used**, and within approximately **20 minutes or less it reached 100%**. When I checked Usage History, I found a very clear change in billing behavior while my session context remained almost the same size. Before the issue: ```text ~529K–531K input tokens/request Cost: approximately $0.0040–$0.0044 per request ``` Examples from my usage history: ```text Aug 16, 9:59 PM Input: 528,969 Output: 230 Cost: $0.0041 Aug 16, 10:00 PM Input: 529,263 Output: 390 Cost: $0.0043 Aug 16, 10:00 PM Input: 529,716 Output: 144 Cost: $0.0040 Aug 16, 10:01 PM Input: 530,924 Output: 168 Cost: $0.0041 Aug 16, 10:02 PM Input: 531,431 Output: 622 Cost: $0.0044 ``` Then suddenly: ```text Aug 16, 10:03 PM Input: 532,116 Output: 144 Cost: $0.1172 Aug 16, 10:04 PM Input: 532,507 Output: 294 Cost: $0.1173 Cache Read: 0 ``` So essentially the same ~530K-token context went from costing around: ```text $0.004 per request ``` to: ```text $0.117 per request ``` That is approximately a **27x increase per request**, without a meaningful increase in context size. The Usage History tooltip explicitly shows: ```text Input: 532507 Cache Read: 0 ``` After this happened, my OpenCode Go allowance was consumed extremely quickly. ### Expected behavior Repeated long-session context should continue receiving the expected DeepSeek cache treatment when the prefix/context has not materially changed. If caching becomes unavailable, there should at minimum be protection against unexpectedly consuming nearly an entire Go allowance in minutes. ### Actual behavior Cache reads appear to have suddenly dropped to zero during an existing long-running DeepSeek V4 Flash session. The same ~530K-token context then began being charged as fresh input repeatedly, increasing individual request cost by roughly 27x. This caused my Go usage to go from approximately **11% used to 100% used in around 20 minutes or less**. ### Impact This effectively consumed almost my entire available Go quota during one short period of normal usage. I did not intentionally create a workload that was approximately 27x more expensive. The cost increase corresponds directly with the apparent loss of cache reads. I have attached a screenshot of the Usage History showing the transition. There are also other reports today involving unusually rapid Go quota consumption, including: * #42871 * #42884 My case specifically appears related to **DeepSeek V4 Flash caching / cache accounting**, rather than simply normal heavy usage. ### Request Could the OpenCode team please investigate: 1. Why did DeepSeek V4 Flash cache reads suddenly drop to 0? 2. Why did essentially identical ~530K-token requests jump from ~$0.004 to ~$0.117 each? 3. Was there a DeepSeek/OpenCode Go backend, routing, caching, or pricing change around this time? 4. Were these requests incorrectly billed as uncached input? 5. Can the Go quota consumed by this apparent cache failure be reviewed and restored? Given that the usage increase occurred directly after the cache behavior changed, I would appreciate **restoration of the Go quota consumed by the abnormal uncached requests** if the investigation confirms this was a service-side caching/accounting problem. ### Screenshot I will attach the Usage History screenshot showing: ```text ~531K input → ~$0.004/request ↓ cache behavior changes ↓ ~532K input → ~$0.117/request Cache Read: 0 ``` ### Environment ```text Plan: OpenCode Go Model: deepseek-v4-flash Date: August 16, 2026 OS: Windows Issue duration: approximately 20 minutes or less Usage impact: approximately 11% used → 100% used ``` ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signals.title: report: cannot navigate into subagents of subagents (only first level works)
signals.text: ## Summary `/report` can only navigate into the first level of subagents in a session tree; navigating into subagents of subagents (two or more levels of nesting) fails with the error "unable to navigate into subagents of subagents - only the first level of subagents work". Diagnostics collection is therefore incomplete for deep session hierarchies, e.g. orchestrator → implementer → nested subagent. ## Environment - opencode version: v0.0.0-next-17403 (opencode2) - OS: Darwin 25.6.0 (darwin arm64) - Terminal: Apple_Terminal, TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor - Shell: /bin/zsh - Install/channel: next - Active plugins: none found in config ## Reproduction 1. Start a session that acts as an orchestrator. 2. Spawn a subagent from that session (level 1). 3. From within the level-1 subagent, spawn another subagent (level 2), so the session tree is nested two levels deep — for example an agent that delegates a verification step to a second agent while it completes implementation work. 4. Run `/report` from the top-level session and attempt to navigate into the nested subagent sessions to collect context/diagnostics. ## Expected Behavior `/report` should be able to navigate into subagents at any depth of the session tree (or at least handle deeper nesting gracefully) so that all relevant subagent context is collected for the issue report. ## Actual Behavior Navigation into second-level subagents fails; `/report` reports that it can only navigate into the first level of subagents ("unable to navigate into subagents of subagents - only the first level of subagents work"). Deeper subagent context is excluded from the collected diagnostics. ## Additional Context - One concrete scenario: an automated build-orchestration workflow that spawns an implementation subagent which itself spawns a verification subagent. When the user runs `/report` mid-workflow, only the top level and the first subagent level are navigable. - Frequency: consistent for nested (subagent-in-subagent) hierarchies; flat, single-level subagent trees are unaffected. - No workaround found yet beyond manually pasting the deeper subagent transcript into the report body.

signals.title: [DecimalError] Invalid argument: [object Object] — non-numeric provider cost field aborts the turn (fatal on `opencode acp`)
signals.text: ### Description `Session.getUsage` throws `[DecimalError] Invalid argument: [object Object]` when a provider's `model.cost` payload carries a non-numeric field. Seen with the `zai-coding-plan` provider (GLM models). - CLI: cosmetic — the error prints after the answer is already out. - `opencode acp`: **fatal** — a tool-using turn aborts mid-flight, which breaks any ACP client (Zed, or automation driving `opencode acp`). Cause: cost is computed by feeding provider-supplied values straight into `decimal.js` (`packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts`, the `new Decimal(tokens.x).mul(costInfo?.y ?? 0)` block). Those fields are declared `Schema.Finite` in `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts`, but the raw models.dev / provider payload is never decoded against that schema before use, and `?? 0` only guards `null`/`undefined`. So a non-numeric value reaches `new Decimal(...)` / `.mul(...)` and throws, taking the turn with it. Reproducible at unit level on current `dev`: call `getUsage` with a model whose `cost.input` is `{}` and it throws ``` [DecimalError] Invalid argument: [object Object] at getUsage (packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts:398:51) ``` Same error string as #6010 (closed); this is the `model.cost` operand path, which still throws. ### OpenCode version 1.18.16, and reproduces on current `dev`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. `opencode run "hi" -m zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3` 2. Or run any tool-using prompt under `opencode acp`. 3. → `[DecimalError] Invalid argument: [object Object]` (logged as `service=session.prompt`); under ACP the turn aborts. ### Operating System macOS (Darwin 25.5.0) ### Terminal VS Code integrated terminal; also reproduced via `opencode acp` driven by an ACP client.

signals.title: write/edit/apply_patch filePath argument not trimmed — local models create files with trailing whitespace in names
signals.text:
## Bug The `write`, `edit`, and `apply_patch` tools pass the `filePath` argument through verbatim without trimming surrounding whitespace. Local models (e.g. Ollama Gemma) that emit a trailing `
` inside the JSON string argument end up creating files whose names literally contain a newline character, e.g. `ruleset.md
` instead of `ruleset.md`. ## Reproduction Config: Ollama provider with `gemma-4-12B-code:latest`, `general` subagent model override, LitRPG skill setup that writes 10 state files. Model emitted a tool call resembling: ```json {"name": "write", "arguments": {"filePath": "/tmp/opencode/litrpg-gemma-test/ruleset.md
", "content": "..."}} ``` Result — all 10 files created with a trailing `
` in their names: ``` $ ls -lab /tmp/opencode/litrpg-gemma-test/ -rw-r--r-- 1237 Aug 17 ruleset.md
 -rw-r--r-- 392 Aug 17 stats.md
 ... (all 10 files affected) ``` Hex of a filename tail confirms the literal newline: ``` $ printf '%s' "ruleset.md
" | tail -c 5 | od -An -c r . m d 
 ``` opencode's own log shows the un-trimmed path at write time: ``` message="touching file" file="/tmp/opencode/litr_gemma_test/inventory.md
" message=evaluated permission=edit pattern="../../../../tmp/opencode/litr_gemma_test/inventory.md
" ``` The files are effectively invisible to normal `ls`/`cat`/editors and to subsequent `read`/`edit` calls that use the trimmed name, so the model thinks its writes succeeded but the files are unreachable. ## Expected behavior Trim leading/trailing whitespace (including `
`, ``, `	`, spaces) from `filePath` before resolving the path, in `write`, `edit`, and `apply_patch`. A model emitting `"filePath": "ruleset.md
"` should write to `ruleset.md`. ## Why this matters - Affects all local OpenAI-compatible models, not just Gemma — small models commonly include stray whitespace in JSON string args. - Silent failure: the model reports success, files exist, but are unreachable by name. Very hard to debug without hex inspection of filenames. - Cloud-hosted models (Claude, GPT) don't hit this because their tool-call args are clean, so the bug is invisible to most users. ## Environment - opencode: latest (1.x) - Provider: Ollama (local), `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` - Model: `gemma-4-12B-code:latest` (Q4_K_M) - OS: Linux ## Workaround Skill authors can add a "path hygiene" instruction to their skill's system prompt (see LitRPG SKILL.md `### When to Write → Path hygiene`) telling the model not to include trailing whitespace. This helps but is a skill-level patch for what should be a tool-level invariant.

signals.title: Web search consent should not mutate user-authored main config
signals.text: ## Reproduction 1. Start v2 with a file-backed `opencode.json` or `opencode.jsonc`. 2. Leave `websearch` unconfigured. 3. Invoke web search and select **Allow** in the runtime consent prompt. 4. Inspect the config file. V2 adds: ```json { "websearch": { "provider": "random" } } ``` Choosing a specific provider or disabling web search also persists the response in the main config. ## Actual behavior An ordinary runtime consent action modifies the first discovered file-backed main config, often the global user config. The update is JSONC-aware and property-level, not a wholesale rewrite. The unexpected behavior is that tool execution promotes application consent state into a user-authored declarative config file. ## Expected behavior Runtime consent should persist without modifying `opencode.json` or `opencode.jsonc`. Main config changes should result from explicit configuration actions. ## Rationale This is inconsistent with other current interactive state: - Normal TUI preferences are stored in `cli.json`. - Permissions and similar runtime state use database-backed storage. - The only other purpose-built writer of the main config is the explicit `opencode mcp add` command. Mutating shared main config can also affect other channels, installations, or strict-schema consumers. For example, older releases such as v1.17.4 reject the new top-level `websearch` key. ## Narrow proposal Store interactive web-search **Allow**, **Choose**, and **Disable** responses in v2-owned database or KV state. Keep the existing `websearch` config schema as an explicit declarative override, with config taking precedence over stored consent. This preserves fixed, random, and disabled configuration while avoiding an unnecessary main-config mutation.

signals.title: [FEATURE]: Extend CodeMode to built-in OpenCode tools
signals.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request # Extend CodeMode to built-in OpenCode tools OpenCode already has an experimental **CodeMode**, but the current implementation is mainly focused on MCP/user/deferred tools. According to the original CodeMode design, built-in OpenCode tools were intentionally left out of v1. I would like to suggest extending CodeMode to support native tools such as: * `read` * `grep` * `glob` * `bash` * `edit` * `write` ## Example This could allow the model to do something like: ```ts const files = await tools.glob({ pattern: "**/*.ts" }) const contents = await Promise.all( files.map(file => tools.read({ filePath: file })) ) return contents.filter(file => file.content.includes("TODO") ) ``` Instead of requiring multiple LLM round trips: ```text LLM → glob LLM → read LLM → read LLM → read LLM → process results ``` ## Benefits This could reduce: * Model/tool round trips * Token usage from intermediate results * Context pollution * Latency when exploring large codebases Ideally, CodeMode should use the **existing OpenCode tool execution path**, keeping the same permissions, hooks, validation, and logging. ```text execute() ↓ CodeMode runtime ↓ tools.read() / tools.grep() / tools.bash() ↓ existing OpenCode tool dispatcher ``` CodeMode should **not bypass permissions or reimplement the tools**. Since most of the CodeMode infrastructure already exists, this could be treated as a follow-up to the original v1 scope rather than a completely new feature.

signals.title: core: V1 migration fails against older previous-channel database schemas
signals.text: ## Summary The V1→V2 migration fails with `SQLiteError: near ",": syntax error` when `opencode-next.db` was created by an older previous-channel build whose `project` or `session` table lacks nullable columns expected by the current importer. The importer reads source rows with `SELECT *` into current TypeScript shapes. Missing properties become `undefined`; raw SQL interpolation emits an empty expression such as `VALUES (..., , ...)`, and the per-session transaction rolls back. Migration remains incomplete and retries on the next server process. This broadens #41341: `fork_boundary` is one affected field, but the compatibility defect applies to every assumed source column added after the source database was created. ## Environment - opencode version: `0.0.0-beta-17519` - OS: macOS arm64; exact Darwin version unavailable from diagnostics - Terminal: Not applicable; observed through packaged Desktop - Shell: Unavailable; diagnostics only report that a login shell environment loaded - Install/channel: Beta - Previous-channel database version: service last registered as `0.0.0-next-16416` - Active plugins: Unavailable from exported diagnostics ## Reproduction 1. Create or retain an `opencode-next.db` from an older V2 build such as `next-16416`. 2. Ensure it contains at least one project and session, and that its schema predates one or more nullable columns expected by the current importer. 3. Start a current V2 server so `V1Migration.layer` runs. 4. Observe that normal schema migrations complete. 5. Observe the background data migration fail with: ```text V1 migration failed SQLiteError: near ",": syntax error ``` 6. Start another server process and observe the incomplete migration retry. ## Expected Behavior The migration should tolerate all supported historical previous-channel schemas: - Existing columns should be copied. - Absent nullable columns should be projected as SQL `NULL`. - Absent required columns should produce a direct compatibility error naming the table and column. - Source values must always be bound safely; `undefined` must never become an empty SQL expression. - Successfully committed sessions should remain idempotent across retries. ## Actual Behavior The importer declares current row shapes containing fields such as: ```text project: icon_url_override icon_color commands session: fork_boundary time_suspended ``` It then reads the old database without adapting its schema: ```ts source.query<NextProject, []>("SELECT * FROM project").all() source.query<NextSession, []>("SELECT * FROM session ORDER BY id DESC").all() ``` For a column absent from the source table, property access returns `undefined`. The destination SQL interpolates those values directly: ```ts sql` INSERT INTO session_v2 (..., fork_session_id, fork_boundary, slug, ...) VALUES (..., ${session.fork_session_id}, ${session.fork_boundary}, ${session.slug}, ...) ` ``` The generated statement can contain: ```sql VALUES (..., value, , value, ...) ``` SQLite rejects it with: ```text SQLiteError: near ",": syntax error ``` The transaction rolls back, including its migration cursor update, so the same input fails again on a later server process. ## Additional Context ### Observed timeline All timestamps UTC: ```text 23:16:52.519 new server process starts 23:16:52.750 normal database migrations begin 23:16:52.771 normal database migrations complete 23:16:54.798 V1 migration fails: SQLiteError near "," ``` The diagnostic window contains one server run and one V1 migration attempt. Client relaunches reused the same server. This rules out concurrent or duplicate migration execution as the cause of this occurrence. The event cleanup is also not the malformed statement. It uses fixed SQL: ```sql DELETE FROM event WHERE rowid IN (SELECT rowid FROM event LIMIT ?) ``` The near-comma failure occurs later, while importing rows from the previous-channel database. ### Static call stack and data flow ```text CLI / Desktop client Service.ensure(currentVersion) starts `opencode-cli serve --service` ServerProcess.start createRoutes Database layer DatabaseMigration.apply normal schema migrations succeed V1Migration.layer forks V1Migration.run read durable `migration.v1-v2` state count/read `<global-data>/opencode-next.db` importNextDatabase SELECT * FROM project SELECT * FROM session source row lacks historical column property read returns undefined tx.run(INSERT INTO project/session_v2) SQL template emits empty value between commas SQLite parser throws transaction rolls back catches cause runtime migration status = error ``` ### Inputs and outputs ```text Input: current destination database older opencode-next.db source table schema source project/session rows Transformation: SELECT * into current TypeScript interface property access for columns not guaranteed by source schema SQL-template interpolation Output: malformed INSERT statement SQLite syntax error rolled-back session import incomplete migration state ``` ### TUI and Desktop behavior Neither UI initiates this migration directly. The server auto-starts it through `V1Migration.layer`. The TUI migration overlay only polls status. Clients may replace a registered service when versions differ, but the observed failure occurs inside one server process and one migration run. ### Related issue - #41341 identifies the same compatibility pattern specifically for a missing `session.fork_boundary`. The implementation should handle the complete historical schema surface rather than special-case that column. ### Suggested fix 1. Inspect each source table with `PRAGMA table_info`. 2. Build an explicit source projection for the supported current shape. 3. Select `NULL AS <column>` for absent nullable fields. 4. Fail early with a named compatibility error for absent required fields. 5. Use bound destination inserts that preserve `null` and reject `undefined` before SQL generation. 6. Add fixtures for multiple historical `project` and `session` schemas, not only the `fork_boundary` variant.

signals.title: Bug: folder picker search anchored to home dir; cannot find projects on other drives (Windows)
signals.text: ## Title: [Web UI] "Open project" folder picker search is anchored to home directory; cannot find projects on other drives (Windows) ### Describe the bug On Windows, the "Open project" folder picker in the web UI anchors its search base to `path.home` (the OS user home, e.g. `C:\Users\<user>`) instead of the directory the server was started from or the current session directory. As a result, even when `opencode web` is started from the root of another drive (e.g. `D:\`), a plain-text search (typing a project name) only searches inside `C:\Users\<user>` and can never find projects located in subdirectories on the other drive. ### Steps to reproduce 1. On Windows, start `opencode web` from the root of `D:\`. 2. Open the web UI → click "Open project" (add project). 3. Type the name of a project that lives on D: (e.g. `fleximetric` at `D:\code\python-demo\fleximetric`). 4. The dialog shows "No folder found". ### Expected behavior - A plain-text search should be recursive relative to the server start directory (or the current session directory); or - The user should at least be able to switch the search base by typing a drive path. ### Actual behavior - Plain-text search is always anchored to `path.home`; projects on other drives are never found. - Server log captured from a real browser request: `GET /find/file?directory=C:\Users\<user>&query=fleximetric&dirs=true&limit=50` → `results=0`. - The exact same query with `directory=D:\` returns `results=50`, proving the backend recursive search works fine — the bug is purely in the frontend search-base selection. ### Root cause analysis In the web bundle (`oc-dialog-v2.js`), the dialog search base is computed with this priority: ```js base = start || path.home || path.directory ``` The dialog is opened without `start`, so `path.home` (OS user home) always wins over `path.directory` (server start directory). The `/path` endpoint confirms the two are independent: ```json { "home": "C:\\Users\\<user>", "directory": "D:\\" } ``` The frontend search only ever uses `home`. ### Workaround - In the search box, first type `D:\` + Enter (or click the Root button) to move the browse base to the target drive, then type the project name to search; or - Type the full path `D:/code/python-demo` and navigate level by level; or - Open the project once in the TUI — it will then appear in the web sidebar. ### Environment - opencode version: v1.18.18 (npm global install) - OS: Windows 10/11 - Note: Chinese (non-ASCII) directory names also show as mojibake in the web UI (GBK vs UTF-8 mismatch) — related encoding issue, worth fixing together. ### Related issues - #6490 — identical report (web UI cannot browse projects under `D:\code\python`); auto-closed after 60 days of inactivity, never fixed. - #32747 — ripgrepLayer only indexes the directory snapshot from server boot; new files require a restart (related but not identical). - #28303 — project picker misses deep WSL project folders (same class of "picker search scope" problem).

signals.title: Sessions created before Aug 14 became unusable after the message ID timestamp rollover
signals.text: ### Description We encountered an actual rollover incident on **2026-08-14 at 11:19:55.136 UTC**. A previously working session created before Aug 14 could no longer be used after the rollover. Every new user prompt was accepted, but OpenCode immediately exited the prompt loop at step 0 without creating an assistant message or invoking the model. New sessions created after the rollover continued to work. Observed OpenCode logs for each failed prompt: ```text session.prompt step=0 loop session.prompt exiting loop ``` There was no provider stream, model request, or assistant message. The failure persisted across process/runtime changes because the pre-rollover messages were stored in the session history. The affected session contained: ```text last finished assistant before rollover: msg_ff... new user prompt after rollover: msg_00... ``` The ID prefix rolls over because the identifier stores `timestamp * 0x1000 + counter` in only 6 bytes. The counter consumes 12 of the 48 bits, leaving 36 bits for the millisecond timestamp: ```text 2^36 ms = 68,719,476,736 ms = about 795.36 days 26 * 2^36 ms = 2026-08-14T11:19:55.136Z ``` After that boundary, a new `msg_00...` user ID sorts before an older `msg_ff...` assistant ID. This makes the following guard true even though the assistant belongs to an earlier user turn: ```ts lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id ``` The loop therefore treats the new user message as already answered and exits without a response. Expected behavior: sessions created before Aug 14 should remain usable after the rollover, and a new assistant response should be generated for the new user message. Suggested fix: determine whether the latest user was answered through the explicit relationship instead of lexicographic ID ordering: ```diff - lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id + lastAssistant.parentID === lastUser.id ``` Please also add a regression test with a finished assistant immediately before a `2^36` millisecond boundary and a new user message immediately after it. Related reports about the same fragile ID-ordering assumption: #11863, #13577, #17012, #18807, and #30809. Those reports cover clock skew, loops, or duplicate replies; this report is specifically about the real global timestamp rollover on Aug 14 causing pre-existing sessions to stop responding. ### Plugins None relevant. ### OpenCode version v1.18.1 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Generate an ascending ID immediately before and at the rollover boundary: ```ts import { create } from "@opencode-ai/schema/identifier" const rollover = 26 * 2 ** 36 const before = create(false, rollover - 1) const after = create(false, rollover) console.log(before, after, before < after) // false: the post-rollover ID sorts before the pre-rollover ID ``` 2. In one session, persist a finished assistant message using the pre-rollover ID. 3. Add a new user message using the post-rollover ID. 4. Run `SessionPrompt.loop()`. 5. Observe `step=0` followed immediately by `exiting loop`, with no assistant message and no provider invocation. 6. Send more prompts to the same session; it remains unusable because the pre-rollover assistant is still in its history. ### Screenshot and/or share link Not publicly available. The issue was confirmed from persisted session metadata and OpenCode runtime logs. ### Operating System Linux ### Terminal N/A — OpenCode server/embedded runtime

signals.title: [BUG]: Primary-agent switches silently keep the previous agent's model in V2
signals.text: ### Description In the OpenCode 2 beta, switching primary agents changes the prompt and permissions but silently keeps the existing session model and variant. For example, with Plan configured for `provider/model-a#high` and Build configured for `provider/model-b#max`, a Plan session remains on model A after Shift-Tab selects Build. The next request runs the Build agent on model A. Delegated children do use their own configured models, so the behavior is inconsistent between primary-agent switching and delegation. This recreates the UX reported in #3550 and previously fixed by #3572. V2 now documents the separate session model, but the result is still surprising: an agent profile combines a prompt, permissions, and a model preference, and the UI presents the agent and model together. This can silently run a role on a weaker, more expensive, or incompatible model and reasoning variant. It can also defeat an intended local-model boundary when a sensitive role is selected after a hosted-model role. There is a legitimate opposite requirement in #41221: a model chosen manually should not be discarded on every agent switch. An unconditional "always switch" or "always preserve" rule makes one workflow fail. Suggested behavior: - Track whether the session model is **following the agent default** or **pinned by the user**. - A new session initialized from an agent's configured model starts in follow-agent mode. - In follow-agent mode, switching primary agents applies the new agent's configured model and variant. - Selecting `/models` or `/variants` explicitly pins the session choice, so it survives later agent switches. - Show when a session override is pinned and provide a simple "Use agent default" action to return to follow-agent mode. - Update the selected agent and effective model atomically so plugins do not need timing-sensitive synchronization hooks. That preserves explicit user choices while making configured role defaults behave like defaults. It prevents silent model/role mismatches without forcing plugin authors to build parallel preference stores or race the TUI. ### Plugins None required. The behavior reproduces with native V2 `agents.<role>.model` configuration. ### OpenCode version `opencode2 v0.0.0-beta-17577` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure two selectable primary agents with different native `model` values and variants. 2. Start a new session with the first agent and confirm its configured model is active. 3. Shift-Tab to the second agent. 4. Send a prompt. 5. Observe that the second agent's prompt/permissions run with the first agent's session model instead of its configured model. 6. As a control, delegate to a child with its own configured model and observe that the child uses its configured model. ### Screenshot and/or share link No public share link; the session contains private repository context. ### Operating System Fedora Linux 44 ### Terminal OpenCode TUI on Linux

signals.title: [OpenCode Go] DeepSeek V4 Flash intermittently degenerates into gibberish
signals.text: ### Description ### What happened? When using `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` through RikkaHub, the model intermittently starts generating normal Chinese text and then gradually degenerates into incoherent gibberish. The degeneration typically looks like: normal Chinese → broken grammar / unrelated word combinations → mixed Chinese, English, Japanese, Arabic and random fragments → almost completely nonsensical output I performed several A/B tests and so far the issue appears to be specific to the OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 Flash route. ### A/B testing Using the same RikkaHub client and the same conversation: - OpenCode Go → DeepSeek V4 Flash: frequently reproduces the gibberish issue - OpenCode Go → DeepSeek V4 Pro: normal - OpenCode Go → Kimi models: normal - OpenCode Go → MiniMax models: normal - Official DeepSeek API → DeepSeek V4 Flash: normal The official DeepSeek V4 Flash API has not shown this type of degeneration in my testing. This suggests the problem may be specific to the `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` serving/routing path or its compatibility layer. ### Context One affected conversation is a long Chinese chat / roleplay conversation. With DeepSeek V4 Flash, the conversation is approximately 200K input tokens. The response usually starts completely normally, but during the same generation it may suddenly begin to deteriorate and eventually become unreadable multilingual gibberish. Other OpenCode Go models continue the same conversation normally. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use OpenCode Go in RikkaHub. 2. Select `deepseek-v4-flash`. 3. Continue a long multi-turn Chinese conversation. 4. Ask for a relatively long response. 5. Occasionally the response starts normally and then progressively degenerates into gibberish. 6. Switch the same conversation to OpenCode Go V4 Pro / Kimi / MiniMax: output remains normal. 7. Switch the same conversation to DeepSeek V4 Flash through the official DeepSeek API: output remains normal. ### Expected behavior DeepSeek V4 Flash should continue generating coherent text throughout the response, similar to the official DeepSeek API. ### Actual behavior The OpenCode Go V4 Flash route intermittently generates severe incoherent multilingual gibberish during a response. ### Additional information This does not appear to be a general RikkaHub issue because other OpenCode Go models work normally in the same client and conversation. It also does not appear to be a general DeepSeek V4 Flash model issue because the official DeepSeek API works normally in my testing. I can provide a sanitized example or screenshot of an affected output if needed. ### Plugins N/A — reproduced through RikkaHub using the OpenCode Go API. ### OpenCode version N/A — using the OpenCode Go API through RikkaHub, not the OpenCode client. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure OpenCode Go as a provider in RikkaHub. 2. Select `deepseek-v4-flash`. 3. Continue a long multi-turn Chinese conversation (the affected conversation is around 200K input tokens with V4 Flash). 4. Ask the model to generate a relatively long Chinese response. 5. The response may start normally, then progressively degenerate into incoherent multilingual gibberish. 6. Retry the same conversation with OpenCode Go V4 Pro, Kimi, or MiniMax: output remains normal. 7. signals.text: ### Description With the **system** theme, the ` File ` label on file-attachment chips in user messages is invisible — it blends into the badge background, leaving a solid colored block (note the `QUEUED` chip below it renders fine): ![file badge label invisible with system theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wesleywwlam/opencode/pr-assets/file-badge-system-theme-bug.png) ### Root cause `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx` paints the label with `fg: theme.background` over `bg: theme.secondary`. signals.title: [FEATURE] Optional quota multipliers (x2 / x4 / x8 / x16) for Go subscription with volume discount
signals.text: ## Feature Request: Optional quota multipliers (x2 / x4 / x8 / x16) for Go subscription ### Context: how OpenCode limits actually work Today the usage model is: - **Free tier**: rolling windows (daily ~200 requests, plus 5-hour / weekly / monthly limits) — `FreeUsageLimitError` / 429 when exhausted. - **Go subscription**: a flat quota that re-fills on fixed windows (5-hour rolling, weekly, monthly) — `GoUsageLimitError` when exhausted. - **Zen**: pay-as-you-go credits used as fallback. There is no "tier ladder" — Go is a single flat plan with one quota size. When a user's workload outgrows it (CI-heavy usage, parallel sub-agents, big refactors), the only options are: 1. Stay on Go and hit the quota mid-month → fall back to Zen pay-as-you-go, which is hard to budget and surprises at the end of the month. 2. Top up via Zen repeatedly — manual and easy to lose track of. There is no way to "pay a bit more and get exactly 2× the same quota". ### Proposed feature Add an optional **quota multiplier** to the Go subscription: **x1 (default), x2, x4, x8, x16**. The multiplier scales **all Go quota windows** (5-hour rolling, weekly, monthly) by the same factor, and the monthly price scales accordingly — ideally with a modest volume discount at higher multipliers (e.g. x2 = 1.9×, x4 = 3.6×, x8 = 6.8×, x16 = 12.8× of the base Go price). Key requirements: - **Choose the multiplier at checkout** (e.g. "Go x4") and change it any time mid-cycle, prorated. - **Transparent pricing**: show the scaled quota for each window (5h / weekly / monthly) and the exact monthly price before confirming. - **All quota windows scale together** — no option to scale only one window. - **Optional and non-breaking**: existing Go subscribers keep their x1 plan untouched. - **Cleaner than Zen fallback**: the scaled quota re-fills on the same schedule as Go, so usage stays predictable and budgetable. ### Use cases - Solo developer: base Go quota is enough 80% of the time, but some weeks need 2× — switches to Go x2 for that period instead of paying Zen on top. - Small team sharing one subscription: x4 covers a spike month without moving to a different billing model. - CI / automation workloads: predictably high volume → x8 / x16 with a volume discount. ### Why not just Zen? Zen is pay-as-you-go — unpredictable monthly cost and no automatic quota re-fill. A multiplier keeps the "set it and forget it" subscription model while letting users right-size their quota. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Multiplier selectable at subscription time and changeable later (prorated). - [ ] Price + scaled quotas (5h / weekly / monthly) shown for every multiplier before confirmation. - [ ] `opencode usage` (see #32913) reflects the scaled quotas. - [ ] Volume discount documented and applied at higher multipliers. ### Related - #24879 (Pro tier proposal) — overlaps in the "more quota" goal but proposes a separate tier; a multiplier is orthogonal and can complement it. - #32913 (CLI usage view) — would display the scaled limits. Happy to clarify or help test if this gets picked up.

signals.title: TUI: question tool prompt not visible mid-stream — must interrupt to see it (Solid store key-addition reactivity gap)
signals.text: ## Summary In the opencode TUI (macOS Terminal), when the assistant calls the `question` tool mid-response while tokens are still streaming, the question prompt is **NOT visible** to the user. The user must interrupt (Ctrl+C); only then does the question appear. ## Root cause (corrected after live debugging) **A user-installed global plugin (`~/.config/opencode/plugins/notify.ts`) blocks tool execution on a synchronous macOS desktop notification.** The notify plugin registers a `tool.execute.before` hook that special-cases the `question` tool: ```ts "tool.execute.before": async (input) => { if (input.tool === "question") { applyRuntimeSessionStatusTransition(...) await notifyQuestionIfNeeded(...) // blocks here } } ``` `notifyQuestionIfNeeded` → `handleQuestionAsked` → `sendDesktopNotification` → `sendMacOSAlerterNotification` → `Bun.spawn(["/opt/homebrew/bin/alerter", ...])` → `await process.exited`. `alerter` is a blocking macOS notification tool — it does not exit until the user dismisses the notification. This blocks `plugin.trigger("tool.execute.before")`, so the question tool's `execute` body never runs, `Question.ask` never runs, `Event.Asked` is never published, the `question.asked` SSE event is never emitted, and the TUI never renders the prompt. On interrupt, the worker is killed → alerter dies → the blocked await rejects → the tool aborts. The "appears after interrupt" was the abort path, not a recovery path. ### Why `bash`/`read`/`grep` tools worked The notify plugin's hook only special-cases `input.tool === "question"`. For all other tools the hook returns immediately. ### What was disproved - **"Solid store key-addition reactivity gap"** (original hypothesis) — WRONG. A unit test proved Solid 1.9.10 recomputes the `questions()` memo on key addition. The store reactivity is fine; the event simply never arrived because the tool body never ran. - **"SSE events unreliable mid-stream"** — WRONG. The event was never emitted; the server-side `Question.ask` (which publishes `Event.Asked`) never executed. - **16ms event batching** — bounded, not the cause. ### Corroborating evidence - `globalAskCount` counter in `Question.ask` stayed `0` during repro — the function never ran. - `Tool.execute` wrapper fired for `bash` but never for `question` — the tool body was never reached. - The blocking hook was identified as hook#11 (idx 11/12, keys `[tool.execute.before, event]`) via per-hook tracing in `plugin.trigger`. ## Defense-in-depth fix (this PR) The user-side fix (changing `await` to `void` in the notify plugin) is outside this repo. However, the TUI currently has **no recovery path** for a genuinely missed `question.asked`/`permission.asked` SSE event, unlike the CLI transport which polls `question.list` as a fallback (`packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run/stream.transport.ts:556-598`). This PR adds the same defense-in-depth to the TUI so a missed event (network blip, slow hydration, plugin misbehavior) does not leave the prompt invisible. ### Changes 1. **`packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx`** — `recoverPending(kind, sessionID, partID, messageID)`: when a tool part is `running` and the corresponding `question`/`permission` store key is empty, poll the v1 `question.list`/`permission.list` endpoints every 250ms until the prompt appears, the part finishes, or the context unmounts. Mirrors the CLI's `recoverQuestion`. Gated on `permission.mode !== "auto"` for the permission branch (auto mode auto-replies and never stores). Also extends `sync.session.sync` to pre-initialize the keys on session open (cold-start). 2. **`packages/tui/src/context/sdk.tsx`** — bypass the 16ms event batch for `question.asked`/`question.replied`/`question.rejected`/`permission.asked`/`permission.replied` so they flush immediately. 3. **Tests** — 4 integration tests (`sync-recovery.test.tsx`) and 4 unit tests (`solid-reactivity.test.ts`). ## Environment - opencode: `1.18.15` (dev branch, HEAD `4e81a0b`) - Interface: TUI (macOS Terminal) - OS: macOS (Darwin) ## Repro 1. Install the notify plugin (or any plugin with a blocking `tool.execute.before` hook for the `question` tool). 2. Start a TUI session with a prompt that causes the assistant to call `question` mid-response. 3. Observe no question prompt is visible; the stream appears stuck. 4. Press Ctrl+C — the question appears (abort path). ## Will submit PR Yes — defense-in-depth TUI recovery, matching the CLI transport's existing pattern.

signals.title: Feature: /cd command to switch working directory of a running session
signals.text: ## Problem When working with multiple git worktrees in parallel, opencode shows the git status of the directory it was started in. Switching to a different worktree requires restarting the session, losing conversation context. ## Proposed Solution A \/cd <directory>\ slash command that switches the working directory of the current session to a different worktree path without restarting. The implementation leverages the existing \xperimental.controlPlane.moveSession\ API: 1. Calls \moveSession\ with the target directory (no change migration, just location switch) 2. Sends a system-reminder to the session about the new directory 3. Refreshes VCS state so the footer/status bar updates ## Example Implementation A TUI plugin at \packages/tui/src/feature-plugins/home/change-directory.tsx\ that: - Registers a \/cd\ slash command via \pi.keymap.registerLayer\ - Opens a dialog with current directory + input field - On submit, calls \sdk.client.experimental.controlPlane.moveSession\ + \sdk.client.session.promptAsync\ with a synthetic reminder - Refreshes VCS via \sdk.client.vcs.get\ Commits on branch \dir-switch\ in a worktree at \.worktrees/dir-switch\. ## Related - \packages/core/src/control-plane/move-session.ts\ — existing MoveSession API (currently only used by the Move dialog) - \packages/tui/src/component/prompt/move.tsx\ — existing move flow (heavier, includes change migration) - \packages/tui/src/context/sync.tsx:534\ — VCS state loaded once at bootstrap, only updated on \ cs.branch.updated\ event

signals.text: ## Summary In the opencode prompt input, `Shift+Enter` submits the message instead of inserting a newline. Since plain `Enter` also submits, there is currently no way to enter multi-line prompts, which significantly limits prompt formatting. ## Environment - opencode version: 1.18.18 - OS: Darwin 24.6.0 (darwin arm64) - Terminal: Ghostty; TERM=xterm-256color; COLORTERM=truecolor - Shell: /bin/zsh - Install/channel: Release channel appears likely; exact channel unavailable - Active plugins: @knikolov/opencode-plugin-simple-memory; no local workspace plugin files found ## Reproduction 1. Open opencode and focus the prompt input. 2. Type text. 3. Press `Shift+Enter`. 4. Observe that the message is submitted instead of a newline being inserted. ## Expected Behavior `Enter` should submit the prompt, while `Shift+Enter` should insert a newline without submitting the message. ## Actual Behavior Both `Enter` and `Shift+Enter` submit the prompt.
