signal.title: `opencode web` shows `ENOENT: xdg-open` error in container environments
signal.text: ## Description Running `opencode web` inside a container (Docker/Podman) without a desktop environment prints an ugly `ENOENT` error because `xdg-open` is not present in the image. The full error: ``` 662 | var file = this.spawnfile = options.file, spawnargs; 663 | if (options.args === @undefined) 664 | spawnargs = this.spawnargs = []; 665 | else 666 | validateArray(options.args, "options.args"), spawnargs = this.spawnargs = options.args; 667 | if (this.#handle = Bun.spawn({ Error: Executable not found in $PATH: "xdg-open" path: "xdg-open", errno: -2, syscall: "spawn xdg-open", code: "ENOENT" at spawn (node:child_process:667:35) at spawn (node:child_process:14:39) at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-8mgmcy90.js:3:5152) ``` ### Update (1.17.3) Since **1.17.3** the HTTP server **does start** even when `xdg-open` is missing — the crash in 1.17.1 was fixed on 1.17.3. However, the error is still printed to stderr on startup, which is noisy and confusing for users running in containers. The error has no useful meaning in a container environment: there is no desktop session, no `$DISPLAY`, and no browser to open. The server works fine, but the user sees a scary stack trace before any output. ## Root cause When `opencode web` starts, it spawns `xdg-open` to open the user's default browser. In a container environment (no desktop session, no `$DISPLAY`, no `xdg-utils` installed), this call fails with `ENOENT`. In 1.17.1 the exception killed the entire process. In 1.17.3 the crash is fixed, but the error is still logged to stderr before the server starts. The server and the browser-opening logic should be decoupled: a missing or failed browser launch should be silent (or at most a warning) in headless environments. ## Why this matters ### 1. Containers are a first-class deployment target OpenCode's own install page documents `docker run -it --rm ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode` as an official installation method. Containers are also used for: - **CI/CD pipelines** — running opencode in automated workflows - **Remote development** — SSH into a host that runs opencode in a container, access the web UI from the browser on the local machine - **Multi-tenant setups** — isolating projects in separate containers on the same host - **Development environments** — using Dev Containers, Podman, or Docker Compose for reproducible workspaces In all these scenarios, the browser runs on the *host*, not inside the container. The container should only serve the web UI; the user opens it manually from their host browser. ### 2. The web server and the browser launch are separate concerns `opencode web` serves an HTTP interface. Opening a browser is a convenience feature for local desktop usage, but it should not be a hard requirement for the server to start. In headless or containerized contexts, this convenience becomes a blocker. ### 3. No graceful fallback exists There is currently no flag like `--no-open` or `--no-browser` to skip the browser launch. The environment variable `BROWSER` is not checked. The only workaround is either: - Installing `xdg-utils` inside the container (pointless — there is no browser to open) - Creating a fake `/usr/local/bin/xdg-open` no-op script (as done in `Containerfile` in this directory) Neither is a proper solution. ## Suggested fix The browser launch error should be suppressed or downgraded to a debug-level log when `xdg-open` is not found: ```typescript try { spawn('xdg-open', [url]); } catch (err) { // Container/headless environment — not an error } ``` Additionally, consider adding: - A `--no-open` / `--no-browser` CLI flag for `opencode web` - Support for the `BROWSER` environment variable as an alternative to `xdg-open` - A `server.openBrowser` config option in `opencode.json` (default: `true`) ## Workaround (immediate) When you create a custom container and add the standard installation method: Add this to your Containerfile before the `ENTRYPOINT`: ```dockerfile # Create a fake xdg-open RUN printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > /usr/local/bin/xdg-open && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/xdg-open ``` This creates a no-op `xdg-open` that satisfies the executable check without actually trying to open a browser. ## Environment - **OpenCode version:** 1.17.1+ (error persists in 1.17.3, though the crash was fixed) - **OS:** Any Linux container (Debian, Alpine, etc.) - **Runtime:** Docker, Podman, or any OCI-compatible container runtime ### Plugins standard opencode plugin as it comes from the factory ### OpenCode version 1.17.3 but from 1.17.1 exist the issue ### Steps to reproduce Simply pull the standard image: podman pull ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode:1.17.3 and run with the web parameter and the error will be displayed on the screen. But this is my Containerfile ```dockerfile FROM docker.io/debian:stable-backports ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive ENV PIP_USER=true # Pre-configurar tshark para que no requiera setuid (ejecutamos como root en el contenedor) RUN echo "wireshark-common wireshark-common/install-setuid boolean false" | debconf-set-selections # Instalar todas las herramientas: esenciales, build, python, red y utilidades varias RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \ ca-certificates \ curl \ git \ jq \ bash \ file \ unzip \ zip \ gcc \ g++ \ make \ && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* # Crear la estructura de directorios usada por opencode.sh para XDG y PYTHONUSERBASE RUN mkdir -p /home/opencode/.config \ /home/opencode/.local/state \ /home/opencode/.local/share \ /home/opencode/.pythonuser # Instalar opencode mediante el instalador oficial RUN curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash \ && ln -sf /root/.opencode/bin/opencode /usr/local/bin/opencode # Copiar y preparar el entrypoint que decide entre modo web y TUI COPY entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/opencode-entrypoint.sh RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/opencode-entrypoint.sh # Base para paquetes Python instalados por el usuario (persistente mediante volumen) ENV PYTHONUSERBASE=/home/opencode/.pythonuser # Directorio de trabajo por defecto: coincide con el volumen montado en opencode.sh WORKDIR /workspace # Puerto por defecto del servidor web de opencode EXPOSE 4096 # Por defecto se arranca el servidor web en 0.0.0.0:4096. # El modo TUI se activa con OPENCODE_MODE=tui (lo hace opencode.sh con --tui/--no-web). signal.title: [FEATURE]: Per-Provider Quota-Aware Auto-Retry with Configurable Reset Schedule
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ### Problem OpenCode's session retry already parses `retry-after` headers and recognises `FreeUsageLimitError` / `GoUsageLimitError` (see `packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts`), but the handling is essentially hardcoded to the OpenCode Go subscription: - `GoUsageLimitError` already extracts `metadata.limitName` (`"5 hour" | "weekly" | "monthly"`) and `retry-after`, then surfaces it in the UI as *"X hour usage limit reached. It will reset in Y hours."* — but the session does **not** actually wait for that reset; it just retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff. - Providers **other than OpenCode Go** (e.g. users bringing their own keys to fixed-window-quota providers) hit a 429 with no `metadata.limitName` in the body. The retry logic falls back to exponential backoff, exhausts the 5 attempts, and gives up — exactly when the user is most likely to need an automatic wait-and-resume. In short: OpenCode already has the *display* half of quota handling (for Go) but not the *wait-until-reset* half, and the whole thing is only wired up for Go. ### Proposed solution 1. **Generalise the existing quota classification.** `packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts` already has the primitives (`LimitName = "5 hour" | "weekly" | "monthly"`, `retry-after` parsing). Expose them through a per-provider config so any provider can declare its own reset schedule. 2. **Read the schedule from `provider.<id>.quota`, not `provider.options.quota`.** The `options` block is pass-through to the AI SDK (`timeout`, `chunkTimeout`, `setCacheKey`, `baseURL`, `apiKey`, `headers`); quota / retry are OpenCode-internal behaviour, so they belong next to `options` rather than inside it. 3. **Actually wait for the next reset** instead of giving up after 5 exponential attempts. **Config** (extends the existing `provider` block; field names follow the camelCase convention used by `baseURL`, `chunkTimeout`, `setCacheKey`): { "provider": { "<id>": { "options": { "...": "..." }, "quota": { "resetTimes": ["00:00", "05:00", "10:00", "15:00", "20:00"], "weeklyResetDay": "monday", "monthlyResetDay": 1 }, "retry": { "maxRetriesPerWindow": 5, "maxTotalRetries": 50 } } } } **Behaviour when a quota error is hit:** 1. Classify error → 5h / weekly / monthly / transient (reuse the existing `LimitName` types from `retry.ts`). 2. 5h hit → next reset from `resetTimes`, sleep, resume. 3. Weekly / monthly hit → surface a clear *"X limit reached, resets on …"* message; no auto-retry inside the session. 4. After `maxRetriesPerWindow` failures inside one window, queue for the next window. 5. Hard ceiling `maxTotalRetries` prevents runaway sessions. **Backwards compatibility:** providers without a `quota` block fall back to today's behaviour (exponential backoff, 5 attempts). ### Related issues - #43126 — auto pause/resume on known reset time (closest match — semantic of "wait for the right reset" already exists, but no per-provider schema) - #39790 / #39791 — fixed-window quota should not retry blindly - #32423 — provider-specific rate limiting (RPM throttle, orthogonal) - #37412 — `ProviderConfig.options.maxRetries/...` proposal (this extends that schema by adding `provider.quota` / `provider.retry` at the top level) - #21960 / #17648 / #30510 / #41848 — retry has no max attempt count

signal.title: fix(flock): log file-lock heartbeat failures instead of silencing
signal.text: ### Description In `packages/core/src/util/flock.ts:230`, the file lock's heartbeat timer silently swallows all filesystem errors: ```ts timer = setInterval(() => { const t = new Date() void utimes(heartbeatPath, t, t).catch(() => undefined) }, intervalMs) ``` The heartbeat is the mechanism by which the current lock holder signals it is still alive. If the heartbeat write fails (disk full, filesystem error, permissions changed, heartbeat path deleted), the error is entirely ignored. Without a functioning heartbeat: 1. Another process polling the lock may detect the lock as **stale** and steal it. 2. Both processes could then hold the lock simultaneously, leading to **concurrent writes** to the same protected resource. 3. This can cause **data corruption** in the critical sections protected by this lock. **Fix**: Log the error so it's visible: ```diff - void utimes(heartbeatPath, t, t).catch(() => undefined) + void utimes(heartbeatPath, t, t).catch((err) => console.warn("lock heartbeat failed:", err)) ``` ### Plugins n/a ### OpenCode version dev ### Steps to reproduce Cause the heartbeat filesystem path to become unwritable (e.g. permissions change, disk full) while a file lock is held. The heartbeat silently stops without warning. ### Screenshot and/or share link n/a ### Operating System n/a ### Terminal n/a

Write changes to `opencode.json` 2. Gracefully restart/reload the current OpenCode session 3. Return the user to the same terminal instance This ensures configuration changes take effect immediately without requiring users to manually exit and relaunch OpenCode. ### Benefits * Better onboarding experience * Reduced configuration errors * Faster discovery of available settings * Less time spent searching documentation for valid JSON keys * More consistent and user-friendly configuration workflow * Immediate feedback through automatic session reload ### Additional Considerations * Generate the menu dynamically from the configuration schema to avoid duplication and keep the UI synchronized with supported settings. * Show default values and descriptions where available. * Warn users when a setting requires a full restart or may impact active sessions.

Tried VS Code extension AND standalone PowerShell terminal — both affected ## Diagnostic Evidence **Log confirms watcher initializes but never publishes file tree:** ``` file.watcher directory=C:\...\project init file.watcher platform=win32 backend=windows watcher backend ``` No `file.tree.updated`, `mention`, or `autocomplete` events appear in logs. **`opencode debug file tree` fails:** ``` Error: Unexpected error, check log file at ... ``` **`opencode debug file list` works** — server CAN see files, but TUI mention system doesn't receive them. **`opencode debug file status` works** — returns git file status correctly. **Resolved config shows watcher ignore patterns are applied:** ```json { "watcher": { "ignore": ["build/**", "build-serena/**", ".git/**", ".cache/**", ".vs/**"] } } ``` ## Expected Behavior `@` should fuzzy-search project files and show them alongside agents in the mention dropdown. ## Actual Behavior Only agents appear. Many agent frameworks support this pattern, and it is pretty universal. At the same time, neither Claude nor Codex nor OpenCode support this. The ideal setup would be a yaml file in which I get to specify nodes and transitions, and specify which agent description should be used for which node, and which command-line-tool or smaller agent should be run on each attempted transition, and how a transition failure should be reported back (e.g. just a descriptive error message from the command-line tool acting as gate, or a full rebuttal from a small agent acting as gate). I'm happy to make an attempt to contribute this code myself, but I'd like to discuss the right design and what I should keep in mind first. :-)

signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ## Feature Request ### Summary Allow users to customize the verb displayed next to the spinner in the TUI via `opencode.json`, similar to Claude Code's `spinnerVerbs` setting. ### Motivation Claude Code supports a `spinnerVerbs` config that lets users replace or append to the default loading verbs shown while the model is thinking (e.g. "Thinking...", "Working..."). This is a small quality-of-life feature that makes the tool feel more personalized and fun. opencode currently only lets you suppress the spinner entirely (`-q`), with no way to customize the text shown in interactive TUI mode. ### Proposed API Add a `spinnerVerbs` key to `opencode.json`: ```json { "spinnerVerbs": { "mode": "replace", "verbs": ["Hallucinating", "Vibing", "Summoning demons"] } } ``` **Fields:** - `mode`: - `"replace"` — use only the provided verbs - `"append"` — add to the existing default verbs - `verbs`: array of strings, each displayed (with `"..."` appended) while the model is processing ### Implementation sketch The spinner component (likely somewhere under `internal/tui/` or similar) would need to: 1. Read `spinnerVerbs` from the config struct (add field to whatever struct mirrors `opencode.json`) 2. On init, build the verb list based on `mode`: - `replace` → use only user-provided verbs - `append` → append user verbs to the default list 3. Cycle through verbs on each spinner tick (same as current behavior, just with the configurable list) No behavior change when `spinnerVerbs` is absent — fully backwards compatible. ### Prior art - Claude Code `settings.json`: `spinnerVerbs.mode` + `spinnerVerbs.verbs`

signal.title: Long-running bash commands with large outputs cause truncation and agent retry loops
signal.text: ### Description Long-running bash commands with verbose output are being truncated and/or timed out, causing agents to re-attempt commands instead of polling the saved tool output. This creates serious idempotency issues in workflows where commands should run to completion. **Current behavior:** 1. Bash commands have a hardcoded 2-minute default timeout (`src/tool/bash.ts:21`) 2. Output is truncated at 2,000 lines or 50KB (`src/tool/truncation.ts:10-11`) 3. When output is truncated, full output is saved to `~/.opencode/data/tool-output/`, but agents frequently re-run the command instead of reading the saved output 4. Commands are killed after timeout, even if they would have completed successfully **The problem:** - Commands that produce large build logs, test outputs, or verbose diagnostics get truncated - Agents see truncated output and often retry the command instead of using `Read` with offset/limit on the saved output file - This creates duplicate work, wasted API calls, and potential side effects from non-idempotent commands - For CI/CD workflows, this behavior is unacceptable - commands should never exit until a proper exit code is received **Current configuration options:** - `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` - env var for timeout (exists) - No configuration for `MAX_LINES` or `MAX_BYTES` truncation limits (hardcoded) **Proposed solution:** Add `opencode.json` configuration for these limits: ```jsonc { "experimental": { "bash": { "timeout_ms": 600000, // 10 minutes "max_lines": 10000, // or null to disable "max_bytes": 512000 // or null to disable } } } ``` This would allow users to configure behavior appropriate for their workflows without needing environment variables. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version Current (main branch) ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run a command that produces more than 2,000 lines of output (e.g., `npm install` with verbose logging, large test suite) 2. Observe output is truncated with message about saved file 3. Watch agent retry the command instead of reading the saved output 4. For timeout: run any command that takes longer than 2 minutes ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System macOS ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: opencode export can write session JSON that opencode import cannot read in 1.4.3
signal.text: ## Summary `opencode 1.4.3` can export a session JSON file that `opencode 1.4.3` cannot import again. The failure happens with sessions that still contain legacy pre-1.4 data shapes. `export` appears to serialize that legacy shape as-is, while `import` validates against the new 1.4 schema. ## Version ```bash opencode --version # 1.4.3 ``` ## Repro 1. Export an existing session: ```bash sid=$(opencode session list --format json -n 1 | jq -r '.[0].id') opencode export "$sid" > /tmp/session.json ``` 2. Try to import the exported file: ```bash opencode import /tmp/session.json ``` ## Actual result Import fails with: ```json [ { "expected": "string", "code": "invalid_type", "path": ["summary", "diffs", 0, "patch"], "message": "Invalid input: expected string, received undefined" } ] ``` I also see legacy user message fields like top-level `variant` in the exported JSON. ## Expected result A file produced by `opencode export` should be importable by `opencode import` in the same version. ## What I found The exported file contains legacy-shaped data such as: - `messages[].info.variant` instead of `messages[].info.model.variant` - `summary.diffs[*].before/after` without `patch` I wrote a local converter that: - moves `messages[].info.variant` -> `messages[].info.model.variant` - replaces legacy `summary.diffs[*].before/after` with a schema-valid `patch` string After that conversion, `opencode import` succeeds. ## Important follow-up finding Even after importing the converted JSON successfully, re-exporting that same session still produces legacy-shaped data again, and raw re-import fails again. So import success does **not** appear to normalize the stored session permanently. ## Evidence from one real session On my exported session JSON: - legacy user `variant` fields: `53` - legacy diff entries with `before/after` and no `patch`: `73` After converting the JSON file, import succeeds. After importing the converted file and re-exporting that same session: - legacy user `variant` fields: `53` - legacy diff entries with `before/after` and no `patch`: `73` And raw import fails again with the same `summary.diffs[0].patch` error. ## Likely cause `export` appears to serialize raw stored session data without normalizing legacy shapes, while `import` strictly validates against current schemas. So either: 1. `export` should normalize legacy session/message data before writing JSON, or 2. `import` should accept and migrate legacy export shapes, or 3. both ## Relevant code paths These looked relevant when I checked source: - `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/export.ts` - `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/import.ts` - `packages/opencode/src/snapshot/index.ts` - `packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts`

signal.title: Cloudflare AI Gateway (Unified Billing) rejects `role: "system"` in messages array when proxying Anthropic models — no way to suppress/remap system messages per-provider
signal.text: ### Description ## Environment - **opencode version**: 1.17.8 - **Provider config**: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` pointing to Cloudflare AI Gateway Unified Billing endpoint - **Endpoint**: `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT_ID}/ai/v1/chat/completions` - **Model**: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` - **OS**: Windows / Linux / macOS (reproduced on Windows) --- ## Problem Cloudflare AI Gateway Unified Billing routes requests to Anthropic's backend. When the model is `anthropic/*`, the gateway applies Anthropic's validation rules, which **do not accept `role: "system"` inside the `messages` array**. The system prompt must be sent as a top-level `system` field, not as a `messages[0]` entry. OpenCode injects its system prompt as `{ "role": "system", "content": "..." }` in the `messages` array (via `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` → `convertToOpenAICompatibleChatMessages`). This causes every request to fail with: ```json { "error": { "message": "Invalid value at messages[0].role: Invalid option: expected one of \"user\"|\"assistant\"", "type": "invalid_request_error" } } ``` Minimal reproduction (direct API call) Fails: ``` POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{ACCOUNT_ID}/ai/v1/chat/completions { "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6", "messages": [ { "role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant." }, { "role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: test ok" } ] } ``` Works (system message removed): ``` { "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: test ok" } ] } ``` Note: OpenAI models on the same Cloudflare endpoint (openai/gpt-4o, etc.) accept role: "system" correctly — this is Anthropic-backend-specific behavior enforced by the gateway. ### Root cause In @ai-sdk/openai-compatible, the system role is always converted to: // convert-to-openai-compatible-chat-messages.ts ``` case 'system': { messages.push({ role: 'system', content, ...metadata }); break; } ``` OpenCode passes the system prompt through this path unconditionally. The @ai-sdk/openai-compatible package exposes a transformRequestBody callback at construction time that could intercept and rewrite messages, but OpenCode does not expose this to users (it is a function and cannot be serialised to JSON config). ### Workaround (current) The only current workaround is to run a local HTTP proxy between OpenCode and Cloudflare that strips/remaps the system message. This is unnecessarily complex for a configuration-level problem. ### Related issues - #30381 — Bad input on Cloudflare Workers AI (different cause: array/string content mismatch, but same gateway) - #31156 — stream_options injected on Databricks AI Gateway (same root pattern: OpenCode emits fields that some gateways reject; fix: per-provider opt-out flag) ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: MCP tool schemas with extended format values emit unknown format warnings
signal.text: ## Description When connecting to MCP servers that use extended JSON Schema format values beyond the JSON Schema Validation spec (e.g. `google-duration`, `uint64`, `int64`, `google-field-mask`), opencode emits warnings at startup: ``` [WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "google-duration" for key "duration" console.warn("unknown format 'uint64' will not be validated") ``` These warnings come from two sources: 1. The MCP SDK's internal AJV validator (compiling tool `outputSchema`) 2. The structured `opencode::mcp::registry` logger (processing tool `inputSchema`) ## How we got here Discovered while setting up the Google Cloud Pub/Sub MCP server. On startup, dozens of `unknown format` warnings flooded stderr — one for each tool schema property using `google-duration`, `uint64`, `int64`, `google-field-mask`, etc. Tracing backward: 1. The MCP `Client` internally creates an AJV instance with `validateFormats: true`. Non-standard formats in `outputSchema` cause `console.warn`. 2. The AI SDK's `jsonSchema()` function also encounters these non-standard formats, triggering `[WARN opencode::mcp::registry]`. Neither source is a functional bug — AJV still accepts the schema, just warns. But the noise makes startup logs hard to read. ## Expected Behavior No warnings about unknown JSON Schema format values from MCP tool schemas. Non-standard formats should be silently ignored.

signal.title: AJV schema validation warnings (unknown format google-duration/uint64) from Google Cloud MCP servers
signal.text: ## Environment - **OpenCode version:** 1.17.7 - **OS:** Windows (win32) ## Summary When using Google Cloud remote MCP servers, OpenCode prints AJV schema validation warnings to stderr during startup. The servers and tools work correctly, but the warnings clutter output and cannot be suppressed via any config option or CLI flag. ## Observed Behavior ``` [2026-06-19T02:58:30Z WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "google-duration" ignored in schema at path "#/properties/messageRetentionDuration" in googlepubsub/tools/topics_list [2026-06-19T02:58:30Z WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "google-duration" ignored in schema at path "#/$defs/PasswordValidationPolicy/properties/passwordChangeInterval" in googlecloudsql/tools/instances_list [2026-06-19T02:58:30Z WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "google-duration" ignored in schema at path "#/properties/versionRetentionPeriod" in googlestorage/tools/buckets_list [2026-06-19T02:58:30Z WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "uint64" ignored in schema at path "#/properties/id" in googlecompute/tools/instances_list [2026-06-19T02:58:30Z WARN opencode::mcp::registry] unknown format "uint64" ignored in schema at path "#/$defs/MaterializedViewDefinition/properties/refreshIntervalMs" in googlebigquery/tools/datasets_list ``` ## Affected Servers | Server | Format | |--------|--------| | google-pubsub | google-duration | | google-cloud-sql | google-duration | | google-cloud-storage | google-duration | | google-cloud-run | google-duration | | google-monitoring | google-duration | | google-logging | google-duration | | google-maps | google-duration | | google-compute | uint64 | | google-bigquery | uint64 | ## How to Reproduce 1. Create a minimal config (`test.jsonc`): ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "mcp": { "google-pubsub": { "type": "remote", "url": "https://mcp.googleapis.com/pubsub" } } } ``` 2. Run: ``` opencode --config test.jsonc run "hello" ``` 3. Observe warnings in stderr No authentication needed — the warning fires during schema fetch before any API call. ## What Doesn't Suppress It - `--log-level ERROR` - `opencode serve` (headless mode) - Config `timeout` option - `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-warnings` - Global `"tools": { "google-*": false }` ## Expected Behavior Either: 1. Downgrade the log level from `warn` to `debug`/`trace` when AJV is configured to ignore unknown formats 2. Expose a config option to control schema validation verbosity 3. Register Google's custom format specifiers so they pass validation cleanly ## Root Cause The MCP client validates tool schemas with AJV. Google Cloud MCP servers use custom JSON Schema format keywords (`google-duration`, `uint64`) not registered with the AJV instance. AJV warns for each unknown format even when configured to ignore them. ## Workaround (fragile) ``` opencode run "<prompt>" 2>&1 | Where-Object {$_ -notmatch 'unknown format'} ```

signal.title: feat(client): session sync engine
signal.text:
## What Replaces the TUI's per-session sync path with a deterministic sync engine: `view = render(fold(snapshot ⊕ durable log) ⊕ outbox ⊕ overlay)`. One snapshot fetch hydrates a session atomically; one server-merged stream (`session.log?after=seq&follow=true&ephemeral=true`) replays durable events and interleaves live durable + ephemeral events; client intents wait in an outbox until their durable echo folds in. This removes the class of bugs where optimistic UI, event glue, and refetch heuristics disagree: the durable echo is the only acknowledgment, replay is gapless by construction, and the server now refuses to fake replay it cannot prove. Draft: built as a parallel path for local comparison. The stock `createData` layer is untouched and the TUI switches via a one-line import (`packages/tui/src/context/data.tsx`). ## How **Core (`packages/core`)** - `Session.snapshot` — session, children, inbox, recent messages (default 200, today's first page), and the aggregate `seq`, read in one transaction so there is exactly one watermark (`src/session.ts`). - Typed `SeqUnavailableError` on `session.log` for cursors beyond the head — and, new in this draft, for cursors whose replay range is not fully retained (`Bus.retainedCount`). `events.persist` defaults to off, so the old behavior "replayed" from an empty table and silently desynced the caller; now the client is told to re-snapshot. Cursorless reads keep the lenient contract. **Protocol / Server (`packages/protocol`, `packages/server`)** - `GET /api/experimental/session/:id/snapshot?recent=N`. - `session.log` gains opt-in `?ephemeral=true` (default stays durable-only, devtools unaffected) and the typed seq-unavailable error. **Client (`packages/client/src/solid/engine/`)** - `fold.ts` (580 lines) — pure fold from snapshot + durable events to renderable session state. Enforced pure: a law asserts it cannot reference intents or the engine. - `engine.ts` (440 lines) — outbox, ephemeral overlay, reconnect loop. Intents leave the outbox only when their client-minted ID folds in; reconnect tails from the last seq, and any unprovable gap (typed error or a `log.synced` marker past the fold) recovers through a fresh snapshot. - `engine-data.ts` (215 lines) — transport over the generated client plus a data-layer adapter that keeps the existing Solid store shape, so components don't change. **TUI (`packages/tui`)** - `createData` → `createEngineData` in `context/data.tsx`; a small row-model addition in `routes/session/rows.ts`. No component changes. ## Scope - Session aggregate only. Ambient state (catalog, agents, projects, session list) stays on the existing global bus; the `/api/event` filter param (S4 in the plan) is deliberately deferred. - No deletion of the stock data layer yet. A deletion pass was built and then deliberately dropped during rebase: upstream #42999/#43017 made `createData` the shared Solid data layer for the web app, so the legacy session sync is no longer dead code under the engine — it is the app's live path. Promotion now means moving the app to the engine as well, tracked in `SYNC_ENGINE_PLAN.md`. - Optimistic rows render text/agents immediately; file attachments render fully when the durable echo arrives (the client does not duplicate server-side file loading). - Event persistence remains opt-in (`events.persist`); the engine's contract is complete without it (snapshot + live tail + honest refusal). A retention window can drop in later behind the same check. ## Testing - Engine laws (`packages/client/test/sync-engine-laws.test.ts`): idempotency under lost responses, echo determinism, fold purity, submission-order admission, multi-client convergence to the server fold, failure atomicity, lossy-history recovery, attach-gap recovery, refresh/live-log race. - Chaos simulation (`sync-engine-sim.test.ts`): seeded multi-client runs with lost requests/responses, rejections, latency, and connection cuts converge to the server fold (~15k assertions). This caught a real outbox ordering race during development. - Core: `session-snapshot.test.ts`, `session-log.test.ts` including persist-on, persist-off (volatile), and pruned-retention harnesses. - Suites: core 1850 pass / 0 fail, TUI 729 / 0, server 23 / 0, client green except 3 pre-existing generated-client failures that reproduce on stock v2. Typechecks pass in all touched packages. - Live: exercised end-to-end against a worktree server on the real database (prompt admission with client-minted IDs, outbox settling, snapshot/tail hydration in the dev TUI). ## Performance `packages/client/scripts/bench-session-sync.ts` (`bun run bench:sync`) replays a heavy streaming session through legacy `createData` and `createEngineData`; experiment log in `packages/client/perf/session-sync.md`. - Baseline engine cost was 240µs per token delta (full-view `structuredClone` + reconcile per publish) vs legacy's 0.3µs. - Landed optimizations: identity-diff consecutive engine views (the fold is a persistent structure) and clone only changed subtrees into the store; reference-preserving `render` that remaps only overlay-touched messages; recursive clone instead of `structuredClone` for small per-event subtrees. - Now 3.5µs/delta at 200 messages (69× vs baseline; ~0.035% CPU at 100 tok/s), 23.6µs/delta at 2,000 messages where the remaining cost is the O(n) identity walk. Retained memory is flat (~0.06MB) in both layers. - A follow-up simplification pass (three-agent review) closed the identity-preservation gaps the bench scenario misses: `render` memoizes its durable base on fold/outbox identity and the usage-adjusted session on the usage entry (so streaming stays cheap with a live usage overlay or pending steers), `publish` skips render/notify when folded/outbox/overlay are identity-unchanged, and overlay key parsing moved next to the key constructors. ## Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant TUI participant Engine participant Server participant Log as Durable Log TUI->>Engine: open session Engine->>Server: GET /session/:id/snapshot Server-->>Engine: { session, inbox, messages, seq } Engine->>Server: GET /session/:id/log?after=seq&follow&ephemeral Server-->>Engine: replay (durable) … log.synced … live (durable + ephemeral) TUI->>Engine: submit(text) Engine->>Engine: outbox += intent (client-minted ID), render optimistically Engine->>Server: POST /session/:id/prompt { id } Server->>Log: session.inbox.enqueued { inboxID: id } Log-->>Engine: durable echo Engine->>Engine: fold echo, ack outbox (same update) Note over Engine,Server: disconnect → tail from last seq;
seq-unavailable or marker gap → re-snapshot → resend unacked ```
signal.author: kitlangton

signal.title: Kimi K3: HTTP 400 "assistant message must not be empty" when switching models mid-session
signal.text: ### Description ## Summary When switching to Kimi K3 (Moonshot) mid-session, the next message fails with HTTP 400 because the replayed conversation history contains an assistant message with empty `content` (a tool-only turn). Kimi K3 rejects empty-content assistant messages; Kimi K2 and other OpenAI-compatible providers tolerate them. ## Environment - opencode: `1.18.9` - Provider: Moonshot AI (`/connect` → Moonshot AI) - Model: Kimi K3 — note: K3 is **not yet in the providers docs** (only K2 is documented at https://opencode.ai/docs/providers#moonshot-ai) - OS: `macOS ` - Switched from: GLM-5.2 ## Reproduction 1. Start a session with any model (e.g. GLM-5.2) and let the assistant perform several tool calls (bash/read/edit) — i.e. produce assistant turns that contain only `tool_calls` with no text content. 2. Mid-session, switch the model to Kimi K3 via `/models`. 3. Send any message (e.g. "test"). 4. Request fails immediately with HTTP 400. ## Expected The request is sent to Kimi K3 successfully, or opencode normalizes messages that Kimi K3 rejects. ## Actual HTTP 400 - {"error":{"message":"the message at position 31 with role 'assistant' must not be empty","type":"InvalidParameter","param":null,"code":"InvalidParameter"},"request_id":"9da933b5-c932-959d-b81c-5219bbe9e35f"} The "position 31" assistant message is a tool-only turn (tool calls, no text). opencode serializes it with empty `content`, and Kimi K3 rejects empty-content assistant messages. ## Analysis - opencode (via the Vercel AI SDK) serializes assistant turns that contain only tool calls as messages with empty `content`. - Kimi K3's API is stricter than Kimi K2 / OpenAI / GLM: it rejects assistant messages whose `content` is empty, even when `tool_calls` are present. - This only surfaces when switching models mid-session (full history replayed) or in long agentic sessions with many tool-only assistant turns. - No config option exists to normalize/sanitize these messages — the `provider` options (`baseURL`, `blacklist`/`whitelist`, `options` [timeout/chunkTimeout/setCacheKey/headers/apiKey], `npm`, `name`, `models`) include no message-normalization toggle (https://opencode.ai/docs/config). ## Workarounds - `/clear` or start a new session before using Kimi K3 (history no longer contains the empty assistant turns). - Use Kimi K2 (documented, tolerates empty content) or another provider until K3 is officially supported. ## Suggested fix - Normalize assistant messages before sending to Kimi/Moonshot: when an assistant message has `tool_calls` and empty `content`, send `content: null` (OpenAI-compatible) or a single-space placeholder instead of an empty string — whichever Kimi K3 accepts. - Make this automatic for the Moonshot provider, or expose a per-provider option (e.g. `options.normalizeEmptyAssistantContent`). - Add Kimi K3 to the providers docs / Models.dev metadata once stable. ## References - Providers docs: https://opencode.ai/docs/providers#moonshot-ai (only Kimi K2) - Config docs: https://opencode.ai/docs/config ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version 1.18.9 ### Steps to reproduce _No response_ ### Screenshot and/or share link ### Operating System macOs 26.5.1 (25F80) ### Terminal zsh

signal.title: core: adapt tool-result media placement per provider protocol
signal.text: ## Summary V2 filters media by model input capability, but does not separately account for whether the selected provider protocol can represent that media inside a tool result. A vision-capable model can therefore receive a valid tool-result image at the canonical layer while its provider adapter cannot place that image in the protocol-native tool-result shape. ## Environment - opencode version: V2 development branch - OS: Not environment-specific - Terminal: Not applicable - Shell: Not applicable - Install/channel: V2 development - Active plugins: Not applicable ## Reproduction 1. Select a model that supports image input through a provider protocol that cannot carry images inside tool results. 2. Have the model call a local tool such as `read` that returns an image. 3. Continue the session so the tool result is included in the next model request. ## Expected Behavior Request preparation should distinguish model modality support from provider tool-result placement support. When the model supports the media but the protocol cannot carry it inside a tool result, preserve textual tool output and inject the media through a synthetic user message or another protocol-supported placement. ## Actual Behavior The existing capability filter preserves the image because the model supports image input. The generic bridge then emits typed tool-result media, leaving provider adapters that cannot represent that placement to reject, omit, or mishandle it. ## Additional Context This is separate from unsupported-model handling in `SessionModelRequest.unsupportedParts`, which correctly replaces media with explanatory text when the model lacks that modality. The placement policy should live above the generic AI SDK bridge and should cover images and other supported media types according to provider protocol capabilities. V1 has related provider-specific extraction and synthetic-user behavior in `packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts`. Related PR: #41672

signal.title: fix(core): resolve Windows shells installed as app-execution aliases
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #41426 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix ### What does this PR do? On Windows, a configured `shell: "pwsh"` is silently ignored and commands run under PowerShell 5.1 instead. When PowerShell 7 is installed from the Store/MSIX package, `pwsh` on PATH is a Windows **app-execution alias**: a zero-byte `AppExecLink` reparse point, not a real executable. `CreateProcess` resolves it by name, but `stat` does not see it. `Shell.resolve()` goes through `which()`, which stats candidates, so the alias resolves to nothing and `select()` falls back to `win()[0]` — Windows PowerShell 5.1 — without reporting that the configured shell was not found. Measured on Windows 11 with a Store-installed alias: ``` fs.existsSync(<alias>) -> false fs.statSync(<alias>) -> undefined spawnSync("winget", ...) -> status 0 ``` When `which()` finds nothing on Windows for a name we already recognise as a shell, this falls back to `where.exe`, which does resolve aliases, and returns the bare name so `CreateProcess` performs the lookup. `where.exe` distinguishes the two cases cleanly: exit 0 for an installed alias (`winget`), exit 1 for something genuinely absent (`pwsh` when not installed, `zsh`, `ksh`). The fallback is deliberately narrow — Windows only, only after `which()` has already failed, and only for names in the existing shell table — so an unrelated missing binary still resolves to `undefined` as before. ### How did you verify your code works? - Added a test asserting a shell name that resolves to nothing stays `undefined`, guarding the case where `where.exe` might otherwise return a non-shell match. - `bun test test/shell.test.ts` in `packages/core` passes (12/12), and the dependent `shell`/`bash` tool suites in `packages/opencode` still pass. - Verified the alias behaviour directly on Windows 11 with the numbers above, using `winget` as a stand-in alias, and confirmed `where.exe` exits 1 for shells that are actually absent. - `bun typecheck` passes. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: Windows: bash tool ignores shell: pwsh config — always runs PowerShell 5.1 (1.18.15)
signal.text: **Environment** - Windows 11 24H2, opencode 1.18.15 (desktop/TUI) - PowerShell 7.6.2 installed via Store (MSIX, `WindowsApps` app-execution alias) **Problem** The `shell` config option is documented as *"Default shell to use for terminal and bash tool"* and the docs state *"Compatible shells are also used for agent tool calls"*. On Windows, however, the built-in **bash tool always runs Windows PowerShell 5.1** regardless of the configured shell. **Evidence** 1. Global config `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` contains `"shell": "pwsh"` (confirmed loaded): ``` > opencode debug config "shell": "pwsh", ``` 2. `pwsh` is resolvable and spawnable from Node (same mechanism opencode uses): ``` spawnSync('pwsh', ['-NoProfile','-Command','Write-Output hi']) → status 0, stdout "hi" ``` 3. Yet the agent bash tool executes as PowerShell 5.1: ``` $PSVersionTable.PSVersion.ToString() → 5.1.26100.8875 $PSEdition → Desktop ``` 4. The bash tool's generated description literally says *"Windows PowerShell (5.1)"* — it appears to use a hard-coded Windows default rather than the `shell` config. **Expected** The bash tool should honor `shell: "pwsh"` on Windows, matching the documented behavior ("Compatible shells are also used for agent tool calls"). **Impact** - `shell` config only affects the interactive terminal, not agent tool calls. - Windows users cannot make agents use pwsh 7 (modern syntax, UTF-8-no-BOM default), which matters for tools like `Set-Content` (5.1 corrupts UTF-8 Chinese text) and `rg`. **Repro steps** 1. Set `"shell": "pwsh"` in global config 2. Restart opencode 3. Invoke the bash tool with `$PSVersionTable.PSVersion.ToString()` 4. Observe `5.1.26100.8875` / `Desktop` **Workaround (agent-side)** Explicitly invoke pwsh per command: `pwsh -NoProfile -Command '...'` (single-quote the inner command to avoid outer-shell variable expansion).

signal.title: v2 plugin: tool input decode breaks when server effect version drifts from plugin's effect
signal.text: ## Summary Plugin-provided tools are silently version-coupled to the server's bundled `effect`. When the managed service auto-updated to a build bundling `effect@4.0.0-beta.107`, every tool from a config plugin built against `effect@4.0.0-beta.101` began failing input decode with `Invalid tool input: Expected object` — input-independent, for every tool, until the plugin's `effect` is manually realigned with the server bundle. Any server update that bumps `effect` can break all installed effect plugins. ## Environment - opencode version: 0.0.0-beta-17595 (managed service, auto-updated mid-session from an earlier beta) - OS: Darwin 25.5.0 (darwin arm64) - Terminal: ghostty (TERM=xterm-ghostty) - Shell: /bin/zsh - Install/channel: beta - Active plugins: `~/.config/opencode/plugins/session-control.ts` (effect plugin; the one affected), opencode-voice agent plugin, debug-workspace-plugin ## Reproduction 1. Install a config plugin that defines tools via `@opencode-ai/plugin/effect` with `Schema.Struct` input schemas, with `effect@4.0.0-beta.101` in the config directory's `node_modules` (`~/.config/opencode/package.json` pinning `effect: 4.0.0-beta.101`). 2. Run a server build bundling `effect@4.0.0-beta.107` (e.g. current beta `0.0.0-beta-17595`). 3. From Code Mode, call any of the plugin's tools with a perfectly valid input, e.g. `tools.session.get({})`. ## Expected Behavior The tool input decodes and the tool runs — or, if plugin/server effect versions are genuinely incompatible, a loud, diagnosable error at plugin load time naming the version mismatch, not a per-call decode failure that looks like caller error. ## Actual Behavior Every call to every tool from the plugin fails with: ```text Error: Invalid tool input: Expected object ``` The error is input-independent — `{}`, a fully valid object, and even a raw string all produce the identical message: ```js await tools.session.get() // "Tool 'session.get' expects exactly one input object." (codemode arg check — works) await tools.session.get({}) // "Invalid tool input: Expected object" await tools.session.rename({ title: "probe" }) // "Invalid tool input: Expected object" await tools.session.get("string") // "Invalid tool input: Expected object" (same message, wrong-type input) ``` Code Mode builtins (`search`) and MCP-backed tools are unaffected; only effect-plugin tools fail. ## Additional Context Diagnosis trail: - The error string originates in `packages/core/src/tool/runtime.ts` `decodeInput`: `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(schema)(value)` — the **server's** effect decoding the **plugin's** schema object. - The Schema `TypeId` string (`"~effect/Schema/Schema"`) is identical in beta.101 and beta.107, so the foreign schema passes `Schema.isSchema` and proceeds into the host decoder, which then fails on the drifted internals (beta.101→107 includes Schema representation/identity changes, the SchemaError move, and AST transform memoization). - Timeline: the managed service auto-updated and restarted mid-day (old pid replaced ~13:12 local); the plugin and its `node_modules` were unchanged for a week. Tools worked before the restart, and all failed after — same session, same call sites. - Workaround that fixes it: `cd ~/.config/opencode && bun add effect@4.0.0-beta.107 @opencode-ai/plugin@next`, then restart the service. This must be repeated on every server update that bumps effect. Suggested directions (any one resolves the class of failure): 1. Decode plugin tool inputs through the standard-schema interface of the *plugin's own* schema (version-agnostic: the plugin's instance validates, the host only transports), instead of running the host's `decodeUnknownEffect` on a foreign schema. 2. Have `@opencode-ai/plugin` re-export `effect` (and document that plugins must import it from there), so plugins always share the server's instance. 3. At plugin load, detect an effect-instance/version mismatch between host and plugin and fail loudly with the two versions named — turning a silent per-call decode failure into an actionable load error.

signal.title: [FEATURE]: Let injected text parts opt into markdown rendering in the TUI
signal.text: ### Feature hasn't been suggested before. - [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before. ### Describe the enhancement you want to request ### Problem A plugin or a tool that posts into a session through `session.prompt` has no way to get its text rendered. Everything sent that way becomes a text part on a user message, and the TUI renders user text through a plain `<text>` node while the assistant path renders through `<markdown>`: ``` packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx 1420 <text fg={theme.text}>{text()}</text> // UserMessage 1700 <markdown ... content={props.part.text.trim()} /> // TextPart, typed message: AssistantMessage ``` So a plugin that reports status back into the session shows raw markup on screen, sitting next to assistant output that is rendered. The case I hit is a background agent plugin posting its completion notice into the parent session: headings, bold and fenced code all arrive literally. The only lever a plugin has today is `synthetic: true`, which hides the part from the message bubble. That is the right call for text meant only for the model, and it does not help when the text is also meant for the person watching. ### Prior issues #5675, #12791 and #21510 all asked for markdown in user messages and were closed. On #5675 a maintainer answered that plain user prompts are intentional, with the door left open. I read that as correct for typed prompts: rendering markdown over what someone typed would eat characters from their own words when they echo back. This request is narrower and does not touch that. ### Proposal Let a text part opt in with `metadata.render` set to `"markdown"`, and render only those through the markdown component. Parts without the flag keep rendering as they do now. `TextPartInput` already carries `metadata`, and `resolvePart` in `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:992` spreads the input part into the stored part, so the flag already survives the round trip. signal.title: tui: let injected text parts opt into markdown rendering
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #43318 ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? A user message renders its visible text through a plain `<text>` node, while the assistant path renders through `<markdown>`: ``` packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx 1420 <text fg={theme.text}>{text()}</text> // UserMessage 1700 <markdown ... content={props.part.text.trim()} /> // TextPart, typed message: AssistantMessage ``` That split is right for text a person typed and wrong for text a plugin injects. Anything sent through `session.prompt` becomes a text part on a user message, so a plugin reporting status back into the session can only show raw markup. The case I hit is a background agent plugin posting its completion notice into the parent session, which lands as literal headings, asterisks and backticks. A text part can now set `metadata.render` to `"markdown"` and get the markdown component. Parts without the flag render as before, so a typed prompt containing markdown syntax is still echoed back the way it was entered. That keeps the behavior a maintainer called intentional on #5675 while giving programmatic senders a way to ask. Why it needs no schema or server work: `TextPartInput` already carries `metadata`, and `resolvePart` at `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:992` returns `[{ ...part, messageID, sessionID }]`, so the flag already survives the trip from the plugin to the stored part. The TUI was the only place that had to learn to read it. The splitting logic sits in `packages/tui/src/routes/session/user-message-text.ts` so it can be tested without standing up the route. ### How did you verify your code works? ``` bun turbo typecheck --filter=@opencode-ai/tui # pass bun test (packages/tui) # 198 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail oxlint (the three touched files) # 0 errors, no new warnings ``` Five new cases cover typed text staying literal, an opted-in part reaching the markdown body, one message mixing both kinds, synthetic and empty parts staying hidden, and an unrecognized `render` value falling back to literal text. I also ran the suite on the base commit to confirm the counts move by exactly the five tests added, and that the one flaky `flock` ENOENT I saw on a first run is unrelated and does not reproduce. ### Screenshots / recordings A terminal screenshot would carry the color attributes, so this is the character frame from the TUI test renderer instead, same content through each path at width 64. signal.title: deepseek-v4-flash via Console Go (opencode.ai/zen/go) stops after text output: no tool_calls, finish_reason stop
signal.text: ## Summary `deepseek-v4-flash` served through Console Go (`opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`) ends the response with `finish_reason: stop` whenever the model first emits a text passage before tool calls. The tool calls never arrive. An agent loop exits mid-task right after the model says what it is about to do. ## Environment - Client: Grok CLI → cliproxy (Responses→Chat bridge) → Tailscale Aperture → provider `opencode-go` (Console Go, `opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`) → `deepseek-v4-flash` - Observed with `reasoning_effort: xhigh` and `max`; streaming and non-streaming. ## Evidence Batch analysis of 15 captured responses on the gateway (one session, same request shape): | finish_reason | count | text before tool calls | |---|---|---| | `tool_calls` | 6 | 0/6 | | `stop`, no tool_calls | 7 | 7/7 | Every early stop has text first; every normal response skips text. The stopped texts end with a colon, for example "…check the tests directory and summarize:". ## Control experiment Same model, same prompt, same tools, same multi-turn history against the official DeepSeek API (`api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions`), with instructions forcing text-then-tool output: 4/4 returned `finish_reason: tool_calls`, text followed by complete tool calls. The model itself continues normally after text. ## Reasoning_content contract is satisfied Assistant tool-call messages carry `reasoning_content` (229/229 on a 465-message request; empty string when no reasoning was stored). The early stop persists. This points to Console Go terminating its generation at the text→tool_calls transition, independent of request shape. ## Related - #39204: same symptom ("model says it is about to continue" then stops) - #35689: reasoning_content contract root cause. Our data shows the stop persists with the contract satisfied, so this looks like a separate defect in the zen/go serving path. ## Ask Please check Console Go streaming generation for mixed text + tool_calls output from DeepSeek V4 (text deltas followed by tool-call deltas). It appears to end the response at the text boundary instead of continuing into tool calls.

signal.title: Session silently stops on empty LLM response (finish: unknown, 0 tokens)
signal.text: ## Description When the model provider returns an **empty completion** (0 tokens, no text/reasoning/tool output, finish reason maps to `unknown`), opencode treats it as a normal completed turn: - the session loop exits silently (`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` breaks on any finish that isn't `tool-calls`) - no error is surfaced to the user, no retry happens - the conversation appears to "suddenly stop" mid-task Observed with the opencode-go gateway (deepseek-v4-flash) returning an empty response: the session went idle with the last assistant message recorded as `finish: unknown` with 0 tokens. ## Repro - Provider returns an SSE stream with no content/tool deltas and an unknown finish reason. - After processing, the loop exits and the session goes idle with no error. ## Expected An empty response should be retried (or surfaced as an error), not silently treated as a completed turn. Related: #40531 (upstream PR with the same fix, currently conflicting with dev).

signal.title: fix(session): degrade undecodable image attachments instead of failing the prompt
signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #43262 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix ### What does this PR do? A user message containing an image in a format the Photon-based resizer cannot decode (e.g. AVIF, HEIC, BMP, TIFF), or an image too large to be resized below the inline limit, made the entire prompt request fail with HTTP 400, so the image message could never be sent. In `createUserMessage` (`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`), `image.normalize(part)` was wrapped in a fail-fast `Effect.forEach` that only caught `Image.ResizerUnavailableError`. `Image.DecodeError` and `Image.SizeError` propagated and aborted the whole prompt. The tool-result path (`processor.ts`) already degrades gracefully with `Effect.exit` + filtering + an `[N image omitted...]` note, so the user-message path was the asymmetric one. This PR mirrors that pattern: when normalization fails, the image `file` part is replaced with a synthetic text note (filename + mime + reason + a conversion suggestion), and the prompt continues normally. ### How did you verify your code works? - Added a regression test that prompts with an `image/avif` attachment. - Before the fix: the test fails with `ImageDecodeError` aborting the whole prompt. - After the fix: the prompt succeeds and the message contains the synthetic "could not be processed" text note. - `bun test test/session/prompt.test.ts` — 57 pass, 1 unrelated pre-existing glob timeout (also fails on clean `dev`), 1 env skip. - `bun test test/image/image.test.ts` — 5 pass. - `bun run typecheck` (packages/opencode) — clean. - `bunx oxlint` on both changed files — no errors; no new warnings in the changed lines. ### Screenshots / recordings N/A — behavioral fix in the session prompt path, covered by the regression test above. ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: Scrollbalken fehlen in den Einstellungen (Tauri-WebView, Linux)
signal.text: ### Description An das OpenCode-Team, beim Einsatz von OpenCode auf Linux (TUXEDO OS, KDE Plasma 6.5.2, Wayland) fällt auf, dass in den Einstellungen der Modellliste scheinbar kein Weg nach unten besteht. Der Scrollbalken wird nicht angezeigt, obwohl die Liste länger ist als das Fenster hoch ist. Ursache: OpenCode ist eine Tauri-Anwendung. Tauri nutzt die WebView der jeweiligen Plattform (unter Linux typischerweise WebKitGTK). Diese WebView malt ihre Scrollbalken selbst und greift nicht auf die System-Einstellungen für KDE- oder GTK-Scrollbalken zu. Die Folge: wer die Liste der verfügbaren Modelle am unteren Ende erreichen will, sieht keinen Balken und muss raten, dass das Mausrad oder die Tastatur (Bild-ab) noch weiter nach unten führt. Das ist besonders ärgerlich, weil genau die Modellliste der Ort ist, an dem Nutzerinnen und Nutzer ihre Auswahl treffen. Wer nicht weiß, dass es weiter geht, glaubt, die Liste sei zu Ende. Vorschläge: Sichtbaren Scrollbalken erzwingen, unabhängig von der WebView-Voreinstellung. Ein Stück CSS wie scrollbar-width: thin (oder auto) plus ::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 12px; } reicht unter WebKitGTK meist aus, um einen sichtbaren Balken zu bekommen. Alternativ eine optische Andeutung am Listenende: ein dezenter Verlauf oder ein Pfeil, der anzeigt, dass die Liste weiter geht. Das hilft auch Nutzerinnen und Nutzern, die keinen Balken sehen wollen. Als Notlösung in der Doku einen Hinweis auf die Tastatur (Bild-ab, Ende) aufnehmen, damit die Bedienung ohne Maus erkennbar bleibt. Getestet mit der aktuellen OpenCode-Version unter KDE Plasma 6.5.2, Wayland, Oxygen-Anwendungsstil. Der System-Scrollbalken ist hier auf 22 Pixel mit Pfeilen eingestellt und funktioniert in Dolphin, Kate und Okular einwandfrei. Nur OpenCode zeigt keinen Balken. Vielen Dank für das Projekt. OpenCode ist im Alltag eine große Hilfe. signal.title: v2: Responses reasoning can abort with "reasoning start before end"
signal.text: ### Description OpenCode V2 can abort a Session with an internal reasoning start before end defect when an OpenAI Responses-compatible stream starts a higher-index reasoning summary part before the previous part's response.reasoning_summary_part.done boundary has been received or processed. The Session execution then becomes idle, but the current assistant message has no finish, error, completion timestamp, or durable session.step.failed event. The TUI therefore continues showing the reasoning spinner indefinitely even though no model request is still running. The relevant error is: Failed to drain Session Error: reasoning start before end: rs_<redacted>:1 at packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts:142 at SessionRunner.publishLLMEvent at SessionRunner.callModel at SessionRunner.runSteps at SessionRunner.drain The failure follows from the interaction between two otherwise reasonable invariants: 1. packages/ai/src/protocols/open-responses.ts tracks reasoning summary parts as active, can-conclude, or concluded. When part 1 starts, onReasoningSummaryPartAdded closes only previous parts marked can-conclude. If part 0 never reached its expected done event, it remains active, and the parser emits reasoning-start(R:1) without first emitting reasoning-end(R:0). 2. packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts intentionally allows only one open reasoning fragment. It treats that sequence as a defect and dies with reasoning start before end. The provider stream is wrapped in Effect.ensuring(publisher.flush()), so failure cleanup closes and persists part 0. This can make the stored reasoning part look complete after the failure, but the assistant step itself is never terminalized. The stream failure is a defect rather than an AIError, so the normal publisher.failAssistant(...) and publishStepFailure(...) path is skipped before the original cause is rethrown. This is intermittent with live Responses-compatible providers because correctly ordered streams include reasoning_summary_part.done before the next part. It is deterministic with the event fixture below. Potential remediation: - Before starting summary part N, force-close lower-index parts whose state is not already concluded, then mark them concluded. A same-index duplicate should remain idempotent. - Apply the equivalent normalization to the GitHub Copilot Responses parser in packages/core/src/github-copilot/responses/openai-responses-language-model.ts, which has the same can-conclude-only transition. - Independently harden Session settlement so an unexpected non-interrupt stream defect durably fails the assistant step before propagating the original cause. The defect should remain visible to tests and operators, but it should not leave an unterminated message or permanent spinner. The issue is still present on V2 commit 044d04df0693624cf69205e8c9412045fda811d5. ### Plugins _No response_ ### OpenCode version _No response_ ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use an OpenAI Responses-compatible reasoning model with store: false. 2. Feed this SSE event order through the Responses protocol and then through a V2 Session model call: response.output_item.added item = { type: "reasoning", id: "rs_1", encrypted_content: null } response.reasoning_summary_part.added item_id = "rs_1", summary_index = 0 response.reasoning_summary_text.delta item_id = "rs_1", summary_index = 0, delta = "First" # Intentionally omit or delay: # response.reasoning_summary_part.done(item_id="rs_1", summary_index=0) response.reasoning_summary_part.added item_id = "rs_1", summary_index = 1 response.reasoning_summary_text.delta item_id = "rs_1", summary_index = 1, delta = "Second" 3. Observe that the parser emits this invalid common-event sequence: reasoning-start(rs_1:0) reasoning-delta(rs_1:0, "First") reasoning-start(rs_1:1) 4. Observe reasoning start before end: rs_1:1 from createLLMEventPublisher. 5. Inspect the Session afterward. Execution is idle, part 0 was closed by cleanup, but the assistant message has no terminal finish or error, and the TUI reasoning spinner remains active. Suggested regression coverage: - Add a protocol test beside the existing multi-part reasoning tests in packages/ai/test/provider/openai-responses.test.ts, omitting part 0's done event and asserting reasoning-end(rs_1:0) precedes reasoning-start(rs_1:1). - Add the same missing-boundary case for the GitHub Copilot Responses parser. - Add a SessionRunner test proving that an unexpected publisher defect produces exactly one durable failed assistant step before the original defect is propagated. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.text: ### Issue for this PR Closes #36761 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? The `subagent` tool described its `agent` field only as "The type of specialized agent to use for this task" without listing valid IDs, so models guessed plausible names (e.g. `explorer` instead of the actual `explore`) and valid delegation attempts failed at execution time with `Unknown agent: explorer`. This surfaces the exact, currently valid subagent IDs to the model. At tool registration the plugin lists the Location's agents via `Agent.Service.list()`, filters to subagent-capable ones (`mode !== "primary"` and not `hidden`, so `subagent` and `all` modes are included), and appends them to the `agent` input description: `The type of specialized agent to use for this task. Available agent IDs: explore, plan, ...` The catalog is Location-specific and mode-aware by construction; per-caller permission filtering is unchanged and still happens at execution time via the existing `permission.assert` in `execute`. The schema otherwise stays a free-form string (agents are runtime-configurable, so a `Schema.Literals` union would be stale). If no subagent-capable agents exist the description falls back to the previous text. The exported `Input` schema is preserved for external consumers; the input factory now takes the agent description so registration can inject the catalog without dropping the `sessionID` continuation field. ### How did you verify your code works? - `bun test ./test/tool-subagent.test.ts` from `packages/core`: 10 passed (added a focused test for `describeAgents`: subagent + all modes included, primary and hidden excluded, empty fallback) - `bun test` from `packages/core`: 1854 passed, 16 skipped (4 pre-existing Ripgrep timeouts under parallel load, pass in isolation with and without this change) - `bun typecheck` from `packages/core` and repo-wide `bun typecheck` (33 tasks): passed Note: prior implementation #36883 was closed by the automated PR cleanup before review; this PR keeps the `sessionID` field that one accidentally dropped and adds regression coverage. ### Screenshots / recordings N/A (not a UI change) ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

signal.title: Bug: Batched MCP tool calls corrupt parameters when using SSE transport
signal.text: ## Description When opencode batches multiple MCP tool calls in a single message and the MCP server uses SSE transport (port 4201), the second+ tool calls fail with "JSON Parse error: Unexpected EOF". The first call succeeds, but subsequent calls receive corrupted parameters. ## Reproduction 1. Configure an MCP server with SSE transport (not stdio) 2. Have the LLM produce a response with 2+ tool_use blocks targeting that server 3. Opencode dispatches the tool calls 4. First call succeeds, second call fails with corrupted parameters ## Error Pattern ``` Invalid input for tool register_update: JSON parsing failed: Text: {"entry_id": {"tool": "register_update", "error": "Invalid input for tool register_update: JSON parsing failed: Text: {"entry_id": . Error message: JSON Parse error: Unexpected EOF ``` The error shows the first tool call's error response text concatenated into the second tool call's parameters string. The parameters should be a JSON object but arrive as a corrupted string containing both valid JSON and error text from a previous call. ## Root Cause Analysis The streaming parser (Vercel AI SDK Anthropic provider) correctly separates `input_json_delta` buffers per content block index — there is no cross-block buffer leak at the streaming level. The corruption happens in the **MCP SSE transport layer** during concurrent tool call dispatch: 1. Opencode sends tool call N as an HTTP POST to the SSE-transport MCP server 2. The server returns an error response (e.g., validation failure) 3. The error response text is somehow fed back into the shared parameter buffer for the next tool call 4. Tool call N+1 is sent with parameters = `valid_json + error_text_from_N` 5. The server receives corrupted JSON and rejects it This is a **client-side routing/buffering issue** — the MCP client does not properly isolate request construction from response handling when dispatching concurrent tool calls over SSE transport. ## Affected Transport - **SSE transport (port 4201)**: Bug present - **stdio transport**: Not affected (serialized connection) - **Streamable HTTP (port 4200)**: Possibly affected (same HTTP POST mechanism) ## Environment - opencode: v1.18.15 (Bun-compiled TypeScript) - MCP server: Python MCP SDK (mcp package) - Transport: SSE via Starlette - OS: macOS arm64 ## Suggested Fix Ensure each `tools/call` JSON-RPC request has its own isolated parameter buffer. Error responses from one call must not be concatenated into parameter buffers for subsequent calls. Consider: 1. Using separate HTTP connections for concurrent tool calls to the same SSE server 2. Implementing strict request/response correlation with unique JSON-RPC IDs 3. Ensuring parameter buffers are constructed fresh for each call, not shared ## Workaround Our MCP server now has a server-side sanitizer that detects and repairs corrupted parameters by extracting valid JSON from the corruption. This is a safety net, not a proper fix — the fix needs to be in the opencode client.

signal.title: core: subagent tool incorrectly requires sessionID
signal.text: ## Summary The V2 `subagent` tool contract marks `sessionID` as required even though the source schema uses `Schema.optionalKey(...)` and the runtime supports omitting it to create a new child. Agents therefore cannot launch a fresh subagent conversation through the exposed tool interface. ## Environment - opencode version: `opencode2 v0.0.0-beta-17595` - OS: Linux 6.8.0-136-generic x86_64, Ubuntu - Terminal: Ghostty (`TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty`, `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`) - Shell: `/usr/bin/zsh` - Install/channel: V2 beta - Active plugins: `opencode-gitlab-plugin`, `@prevalentware/opencode-goal-plugin@0.1.31`, `/home/ahmed/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js` ## Reproduction 1. Start a V2 session. 2. Ask the agent to launch any subagent, such as `explore`. 3. Observe that the exposed `subagent` tool contract requires a `sessionID`. 4. Attempt to omit `sessionID` when calling the tool. 5. The tool-call layer prevents a genuinely omitted value, forcing a session ID to be supplied. 6. Supplying the current parent session ID reaches the continuation path and fails with `Session <id> is not a child of the current session`. 7. Supplying a fabricated ID fails with `Subagent session not found: <id>`. ## Expected Behavior `sessionID` should be optional in the exposed tool contract. A call such as the following should create a new child session: ```json { "agent": "explore", "description": "Inspect workspace", "prompt": "Briefly inspect the workspace.", "background": false } ``` This matches the source description: "Calls without a sessionID start a new conversation." ## Actual Behavior The callable tool interface requires `sessionID`, so an agent cannot submit a fresh-session call without it. Providing placeholder values produces the expected continuation-path errors: ```text Subagent session not found: <fabricated-id> ``` ```text Session <parent-session-id> is not a child of the current session ``` The source schema added in commit `7188d42b997cc512cea45babd889bb4ea1d66fc1` defines the field as optional: ```ts sessionID: Schema.optionalKey(SessionSchema.ID).annotate({ description: "Continue a specific previous subagent conversation by passing its sessionID. Calls without a sessionID start a new conversation.", }) ``` The runtime also correctly handles omission: ```ts const existing = input.sessionID === undefined ? undefined : yield* runtime.session.get(input.sessionID) ``` This suggests the regression is in Effect-schema-to-tool-contract conversion or tool exposure rather than the subagent continuation runtime. ## Additional Context - Reproduces consistently in this session. - The issue appears to have started with `feat(core): resume subagent sessions` (`7188d42`), which introduced the optional `sessionID` field. - Current `v2` head checked after that commit still retains the same `Schema.optionalKey(...)` definition. - No later V2 commit or matching open PR was found that fixes the exposed required-field mismatch. - Suggested regression coverage: assert the generated tool JSON Schema does not include `sessionID` in `required`, then invoke the exposed subagent tool without `sessionID` and verify that a fresh child session is created.

signal.title: [BUG]: (Incorrect) sampling parameters are hard-coded based on model name/id
signal.text: ### Description opencode automatically adds sampling parameters to chat requests for some model names/ids, even if not configured to do so. I think that opencode should not be doing this, or there should be a way to opt-out, or it should be changed to an opt-in setting. The defaults are defined in: ```text packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts ``` Specifically: - `ProviderTransform.temperature()` - `ProviderTransform.topP()` - `ProviderTransform.topK()` They are applied in: ```text packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts ``` The checks use substring matches against the model name/id (lowercased) Current defaults include: - Model IDs containing `north-mini-code`: temperature `1.0` - Model IDs containing `qwen`: temperature `0.55`, top_p `1.0` - Matching Gemini 2.5, Gemini 3 Flash/Pro, Gemini 3.1, and Gemini 3.5 Flash models: temperature `1.0`, top_p `0.95`, top_k `64` - Model IDs containing `glm-4.6` or `glm-4.7`: temperature `1.0` - Model IDs containing `minimax-m2`: temperature `1.0`, top_p `0.95`, top_k `20` or `40` - Model IDs containing `kimi-k2`: temperature `0.6` or `1.0` - Kimi K2.5 variants: top_p `0.95` - DeepSeek V4 Flash models: top_p `0.95` in specific cases I discovered this when running Qwen 3.8 27B locally in llama.cpp and pointing my opencode config at it. The recommended setting for Qwen 3.8 is top-p 0.95, which is being overridden by these automatically generated sampling parameters. (I specify temperature and top-p settings in llama.cpp for the model) This means i need to also set top_p in opencode config to work around this hardcoded value. ### Plugins none ### OpenCode version 1.18.18 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a single local OpenAI-compatible Qwen model: ```json { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "provider": { "llama": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "options": { "baseURL": "http://localhost:8001/v1" }, "models": { "Qwen-3.8-27B": { "name": "Qwen-3.8-27B" } } } } } ``` 2. Select `Qwen-3.8-27B`. 3. Send a prompt to the model. 4. Inspect the request sent to the server. It contains `top_p` 1.0, based on the model key. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System _No response_ ### Terminal _No response_

signal.title: [BUG] Zen balance does not remove free usage cap; paid users still hit 200-request/free usage limit
signal.text: ### Description Users with an active OpenCode Zen balance are still being limited as if they are free-tier users. I tested this with two separate users/accounts. One account had a Zen balance of at least $20, but both accounts still hit the same free usage cap / 200 request limit and received 429 rate-limit errors. The paid/balance-enabled account did not appear to get any higher allowance or fallback to paid Zen balance. This looks like the free usage limiter is being applied before checking whether the account has Zen balance / billing enabled. Expected behavior: * Accounts without billing/balance should be limited by the free usage cap. * Accounts with Zen balance should either: * use the paid Zen balance after the free cap is reached, or * not receive the same free-tier-only limit. * The error should make clear whether this is a free quota limit, Go usage limit, monthly spend limit, provider limit, or Zen balance issue. Actual behavior: * Both free and paid/balance-enabled users hit the same limit. * The paid account still receives HTTP 429 / `FreeUsageLimitError`. * Adding $20 balance does not appear to remove or bypass the free usage cap. Sanitized example error: ```json { "statusCode": 429, "error": { "type": "FreeUsageLimitError", "message": "Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later." } } ``` This is confusing because Zen is documented as pay-per-request after adding balance, but the account still behaves like an unpaid/free account. ### Plugins None ### OpenCode version 1.17.7 Please confirm if needed; this was observed from the client/user-agent during testing. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create or use an OpenCode Zen account with at least $20 balance. 2. Use a Zen/free model such as `deepseek-v4-flash-free` or another Zen free model. 3. Send requests until the free usage cap is reached. 4. Observe that the account still receives `FreeUsageLimitError` / HTTP 429. 5. Repeat with another user/account without balance. 6. Compare behavior: both accounts appear to receive the same 200-request/free usage cap despite one having Zen balance. ### Screenshot and/or share link _No response_ ### Operating System Linux container ### Terminal OpenCode CLI / server environment
